components.name: accordion
components.title: Accordion
components.purpose: A set of disclosures of which one is open at a time, built on details elements that share a name.
whenToUse: For three or more sections of detail about one thing, such as the environment, commands and test output of a run, when the reader wants one at a time and the set should stay short.
When each section's summary can say in a few words what it holds.
whenNotToUse: When the reader compares sections or needs two open together. Use separate disclosures, which open and close alone.
For one section. Use a disclosure.
For panels that are the main content of a view. Use tabs.
For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical inside a closed section fails the hidden-critical-action rule.
Nested more than two levels. A disclosure inside a section is the limit, and a third level fails the disclosure-depth rule.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Each summary is at least 44px tall and as wide as the set, with a rule between sections and above and below the set.

accessibility: The set is a div with the gw-accordion class. Each section is a details element with the classes gw-disclosure and gw-accordion__section, a gw-disclosure__summary as its first child and one gw-disclosure__content after it. Copy the inside of a section from the disclosure component.

Give every section of one set the same name attribute, and a name no other set on the page uses. The browser then closes the open section when another opens. Where the name attribute is not supported the sections open and close alone, and nothing is lost.
At most one section carries the open attribute in the markup. The open attribute is the only state: never toggle a class.
Every summary holds text that says what the section holds. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule. Trailing text such as a count goes in a gw-disclosure__meta span.

Tab reaches each summary in order. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order, and the browser's find-in-page opens the section that holds a match.
Opening a section closes another without the reader asking, so keep nothing in a section that the reader is filling in, such as a half-written form.
A section may hold one more level of disclosure, a plain gw-disclosure with no name. Do not nest an accordion in an accordion.
The component needs no script.

components.name: activity-feed
components.title: Activity feed
components.purpose: A chronological record of what agents and people did, grouped by day, each entry with its time, its actor, a verb phrase and an optional source or excerpt.
whenToUse: For the history of a task, a run or a repository, read from the oldest entry shown to the newest.
When each event fits one line: who did what, and when.
With role="log" when entries are added while the reader watches.
whenNotToUse: For the full exchange with an agent, with prompts, tool output and answers. Use a transcript of messages.
For one tool call with its arguments and output. Use a tool call.
For a list of runs or tasks to open. Use a list with run status rows.
For a message about the app itself. Use an alert or a banner.
accessibility: Use a section with an aria-label that names what the activity belongs to, such as Activity for task 41. Each label is unique in the view.
Inside it, each day is a div with the class gw-activity-feed__day: a heading, at the level the view needs, that names the day in words such as Today, 22 November, then an ol of entries, oldest first.

An entry is an li holding a time element with a datetime attribute, then a p with the actor in gw-activity-feed__actor followed by a verb phrase that names the thing acted on, then optionally one gw-activity-feed__evidence holding a source chip or a short gw-activity-feed__excerpt.

When entries are appended while the reader watches, put role="log" on the section. A log is announced politely, entry by entry, and needs no script beyond adding the li. Keep role="log" off a feed that only changes when the reader asks.

Use role="feed" only when the app loads entries as the reader scrolls and implements the feed keyboard contract itself: each entry an article with aria-posinset and aria-setsize, and Page Down and Page Up moving between entries. The component does not provide that behaviour.

A long feed shows the latest entries. Earlier ones come in through one quiet small button, Show earlier activity, with a chevron-up icon, in gw-activity-feed__more above the first day. While they are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the button and on the section, and change the button's words to Loading earlier activity. Afterwards move focus to the first entry that was added, so the reader continues from there.
For the first fetch, an empty feed and a failed fetch, the section holds a spinner, a compact empty state or an error state in place of the days.
An excerpt is text, never markup, and is short: one command or one line of output. Longer output belongs in a tool call.
Tab reaches the Show earlier activity button and any source chips, in order. Entries themselves take no focus.

components.name: alert
components.title: Alert
components.purpose: A message inside a view about the state of what the view shows.
whenToUse: To tell the reader something about the run, task or repository on screen that changes what they should do next.
To report the result of an action where it happened, when the result should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For a mistake in one form control. Use the field's error message.
When a whole view failed to load. Use an error state.
When a view has nothing to show yet. Use an empty state.
For a confirmation that should go away by itself. Use a toast.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Context the reader may want. Label it Note.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Something finished as intended. Label it Done.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Something will go wrong unless the reader acts. Label it Warning.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Something failed. Label it Error, and say what to do about it.

accessibility: Every alert holds a gw-alert__label naming its tone in a word. The stylesheet draws the matching icon, so tone is carried by a word, an icon and a colour.
An alert that is part of the view when it loads takes no role. It is read in order with the rest of the content.
An alert the app adds in response to something takes role="status" for info, success and warning, which is announced when the screen reader is next idle.
Use role="alert" only for a failure the reader must know about now. It interrupts whatever is being read.
For the announcement to be reliable, add the element with its role first, or keep it in the page empty and hidden with the hidden attribute, then fill in the text.
The title and body are paragraphs, not headings, so an alert does not change the outline of the view.
At most one action: a gw-button gw-button--small inside gw-alert__action. Never primary. Use a link element when it goes to another view.
Do not move focus to an alert. The role announces it.

components.name: app-header
components.title: App header
components.purpose: The top bar of an app: the product name or the current view's title, with an optional back link, actions and a tray for approvals that are waiting.
whenToUse: Once per screen, as the first thing in the page.
With the product name on a top-level screen, and with a back link and the view's title on a screen below one.
With the tray when something, such as an approval, must stay in sight on every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a view's title with its description and main action inside the page. Use a page header.
For moving between the main destinations on a phone. Use a tab bar.
For a message about the state of the app, such as a lost connection. Use a banner under the header.
For the main action of a view. Put a primary button in the view, never in the header.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Scrolls away with the page. Use it when the screen is short or the header holds nothing the reader needs while scrolling.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Stays at the top while the page scrolls. Use it when the back link, the actions or the tray must stay in reach.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: One row, 52px tall, with 44px controls, at every width. The tray adds a row below it only while it holds something.

accessibility: Use a header element. Outside main it is the page's banner landmark, so a page has one.
The product name is a link to the first screen. The view title is the page's h1 when the header shows one.
The back link names where it goes: visible text such as Tasks, or aria-label="Back to tasks" when it is only the icon.
An icon-only action has an aria-label that says what it does and to what, such as Search tasks. Its icon carries aria-hidden="true".
Use a link for an action that goes to another view and a button for one that acts on this view.
Tab moves through the name or back link, then the actions, then the tray, in the order they are written. Enter follows a link, and Enter or Space presses a button.
A long title is cut with an ellipsis. Keep the full title in the document title or in the page, where it can be read whole.
An empty tray takes no space and is not announced. Leave the element in place and fill it when something is waiting.
With the sticky variant, give the scrolling container scroll-padding-top of the header's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.

components.name: approval
components.title: Approval
components.purpose: One request from an agent that waits for the reader's answer: what would run, where, for whom and why, with Allow and Decline.
whenToUse: When an agent is blocked until the reader allows or declines a tool call or a command.
Alone in a view for one request, or as list items in a queue of several.
whenNotToUse: For a request that was already answered or denied. Use a message row in the transcript.
To say how many requests wait. Use the pending tray.
To confirm an action the reader started themselves, such as deleting a workspace. Use a dialog.

variants.name: normal
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The risk line reads Normal risk and what keeps it so, beside an info icon.

variants.name: elevated
variants.use: A request that reaches outside the task's worktree, deletes, or cannot be undone. The risk line reads Elevated risk and why, beside a warning icon, on a tinted band.

accessibility: Use an article with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-approval__title, a heading at the level the view needs. The title says who asks and for what.

Emphasis: when a view shows a single approval, Allow may be the view's primary action, gw-button gw-button--primary. When approvals are listed, each card sits in its own li of a ul and Allow is a plain gw-button, never primary, so a queue has no competing primary actions.

Allow comes first and Decline sits at the far end of gw-approval__actions. Both are always visible, carry data-gw-critical so the checker can see they are never hidden, and are never placed inside a details element.
The risk line always starts with the words Normal risk or Elevated risk and then says why. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so the tone is never colour alone.
gw-approval__command holds exactly what would run, as text, with characters that cannot be seen written out. It wraps, and never scrolls sideways.
Supporting detail goes in a details element with a text summary, such as Show the full request. It holds no control the reader needs in order to answer.

A note on declining is optional. Under the actions, add a details element whose summary reads Decline with a note, holding a labelled field and its own button, Decline and send note. It starts closed, without the open attribute, and the plain Decline above it still declines with no note.

While the answer is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the pressed button, change its label to Allowing or Declining, and disable the other. If sending fails, restore both and add gw-approval__error with role="alert", saying that nothing was allowed.

Tab reaches the summary, then Allow, then Decline. Enter and Space activate each. The component needs no script: the app sets aria-busy and disabled, and removes the card once the request is answered. Move focus to the next card or the view's heading when it goes.

components.name: attachment-chip
components.title: Attachment chip
components.purpose: One file or image attached to a prompt: its kind as an icon, its name, its size in words and a button that removes it.
whenToUse: Above or below a composer, for each file or image the reader attached to the prompt they are writing.
While an attachment uploads, and when its upload fails.
whenNotToUse: For a reference to a file in the repository, a page or a commit. Use a source chip, which is a link.
For a file listed in a sent message or a changed-files list. Use a dense list.
For a status. Use a badge.
For choosing the file. Use the browser's file input, labelled as a field.

variants.name: file
variants.use: The file icon, for anything that is not an image.

variants.name: image
variants.use: The image icon, with a gw-visually-hidden span reading Image before the name, so the kind is not the icon alone.

accessibility: Each chip is an li with the class gw-attachment-chip, in a ul with an aria-label such as Attachments. Lay the ul out with gw-cluster gw-gap-md: the 12px gap keeps the remove buttons' 44px pointer targets on two rows from overlapping.

Write the whole file name as text, split into gw-attachment-chip__start and gw-attachment-chip__end with no white space between the spans. The end part is the last few characters with the extension. The stylesheet cuts the middle from view only, so a screen reader still reads the whole name.
Write the size with its unit, such as 48 KB or 2.1 MB.

The remove control is a button element with type="button" and the class gw-attachment-chip__remove, holding the x icon with aria-hidden="true" and a gw-visually-hidden span that names the file: Remove session-trace.log. It is drawn 24px square and its pointer target is 44px each way.

While the file uploads, set aria-busy="true" on the li and add a native progress element with the class gw-attachment-chip__progress as its last child, with value and max set from the upload and an aria-label such as Uploading session-trace.log. Leave value off until the first figure arrives. Put the percentage and the size in gw-attachment-chip__size, and name the button Cancel the upload of and the file.

When the upload fails, remove aria-busy and the progress element and add a p with the class gw-attachment-chip__error and role="alert" as the last child. It says what happened and what to do, such as Not attached: files can be up to 10 MB. Remove it and attach a smaller file. Its icon and the chip's outline are drawn by the stylesheet.
While the prompt is being sent, set the disabled attribute on each remove button.
After a chip is removed, move focus to the next chip's remove button, or to the composer when none is left.
Tab reaches each remove button. Enter and Space activate it. The component needs no script of its own: the app sets aria-busy, the progress value, the text and the disabled attribute.

components.name: avatar
components.title: Avatar
components.purpose: A small square mark for a person or an agent, holding initials, an icon or an image, with the name beside it.
whenToUse: To say who did something or who something belongs to: the author of a message, the actor of an event, the owner of a task.
With an icon for an agent and initials or an image for a person, so the two are told apart by shape as well as by name.
With the small size in a dense row, a timeline entry or a line of text.
whenNotToUse: As decoration, or in a stack of overlapping marks. Write the names, or a count such as 4 reviewers.
Without a name, unless the name is already written directly beside it. Then give the mark an accessible name.
For a repository, a branch or a file. Use text, with an icon in a list row where it helps.
For a status. Use a badge. The mark carries no tone and no status dot.

variants.name: initials
variants.use: The default. One or two capital letters in a span with the class gw-avatar__mark.

variants.name: icon
variants.use: An svg with the class gw-avatar__icon inside the mark, for an agent or a system actor.

variants.name: image
variants.use: An img with the class gw-avatar__mark in place of the span. It needs an alt attribute, width and height. The picture is cropped to the square.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: A 32px mark with the name in medium weight.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: A 24px mark with the name at normal weight, for dense rows and lines of text.

accessibility: Use a span with the class gw-avatar holding the mark and then the name in a span with the class gw-avatar__name. The name is visible by default and is what a screen reader reads.
Beside a visible name the mark is decoration: give a span mark aria-hidden="true", and an image mark alt="". The alt attribute is always present on an img.
With no visible name, the mark must carry the name: role="img" and aria-label on a span mark, or the name as the alt text of an image mark.
Say what kind of actor it is in words when it matters, such as Claude Code, implementer. The icon alone does not say it.
If an image fails to load, replace the img with the initials span. The stylesheet cannot do this.
An avatar is not focusable and takes no press. To link to a profile, put the whole avatar inside a link.
The avatar needs no script.

components.name: banner
components.title: Banner
components.purpose: One message about the state of the whole app, across the full width under the app header.
whenToUse: For a condition that affects every screen and is still true, such as a lost connection, a paused agent host or a session about to end.
Directly under the app header, across the full width, for as long as the condition lasts.
With one action when there is one thing the reader can do about it, such as Retry.
whenNotToUse: For the result of something the reader just did, such as Task saved. Confirm it where it happened, or use a toast.
For a problem with one field or one form. Use the field's error message.
For a problem with one item in a view, such as a failed run. Show it on that item.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.
For more than one message at a time. Show the most severe one.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Something the reader should know that needs no action, such as a planned restart or a restored connection. Set role="status".

variants.name: warning

variants.name: danger

accessibility: Set role="status" on an info or warning banner, so a screen reader announces it when the reader pauses. Set role="alert" on a danger banner, so it is announced at once.

Do not set aria-busy on the banner. A screen reader holds back the announcement of a busy region. While the action runs, set aria-busy="true" on the action button and change its label, such as Retrying.
The stylesheet draws the tone's icon, so the tone never depends on colour and needs no markup. The text carries the whole message.

The action and the dismiss button sit together in a gw-banner__actions element after the text. The action is one gw-button gw-button--small, with a label that says what it does. Do not make it primary.
The dismiss button is a button with aria-label="Dismiss", and its icon carries aria-hidden="true". Offer it only when the message is safe to lose. When it is pressed, move focus to the main content.
Tab reaches the action and then the dismiss button, in that order. Enter and Space press them.
The banner does not take focus when it appears, so it never interrupts typing.

components.name: calendar
components.title: Calendar
components.purpose: One month as a grid of days, for picking a single day.
whenToUse: To pick a day near today where the weekday matters, such as the day a scheduled run starts or the day a report begins.
Inside a popover or a sheet opened from a field, or straight in a form.
whenNotToUse: For a date the reader already knows, such as a date of birth or a date far from today. Use a text input with type="date" in a field.
For a time of day. Use a text input with type="time" or a select.
For a choice from a few fixed periods, such as the last 7 or 30 days. Use a segmented control or a select.
To show what happened on each day. This is a picker, not a schedule: use a list or a table grouped by day.

variants.name: buttons
variants.use: The default. A plain table whose days are buttons with aria-pressed. It works with no script beyond handling the press.

variants.name: grid
variants.use: The same markup with role="grid" on the table, aria-selected on the selected day's cell and one day in the tab order. Use it when the app provides the arrow keys.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Each day is 44px tall and at least 44px wide. The month is 308px to 352px wide, which fits a 390px phone with its margins.

accessibility: Use a div with gw-calendar, role="group" and an aria-label that says what the day is for, such as Day the report starts. It holds gw-calendar__header, the table and gw-calendar__status.

gw-calendar__header holds the previous-month button, a p with gw-calendar__title and aria-live="polite" naming the month and year, and the next-month button. Each button is a quiet icon button whose aria-label names the month it goes to: Previous month, October 2026. When the month changes the app rewrites the title and the table, and the title is announced.

The month is a table with gw-calendar__grid and aria-labelledby pointing at the title. Its thead has one th with scope="col" and gw-calendar__weekday for each weekday, holding a two-letter name with aria-hidden="true" and the full name in a gw-visually-hidden span. Each week is a tr of seven td. A cell outside the month is an empty td.

Each day is a button with type="button" and gw-calendar__day, showing the day's number. Its aria-label is the full date with the weekday: Tuesday 24 November 2026. The app writes these, so the stylesheet holds no date arithmetic.

Today carries aria-current="date", and its aria-label ends with the word today: Sunday 22 November 2026, today. The stylesheet draws a ring on it, so today is marked by a shape for the eye and in words for a screen reader.

The selected day carries aria-pressed="true" and every other day aria-pressed="false". The app also writes the choice in words into gw-calendar__status, a p with role="status": Chosen: Tuesday 24 November 2026.

A day that cannot be chosen has the disabled attribute and is struck through. Say why near the calendar, such as Runs can be scheduled from today. Disable the previous-month or next-month button when every day that way is unavailable.
With no script the keyboard still works: Tab moves through the two month buttons and every day, and Enter or Space chooses a day.

The arrow keys are the app's to provide, with the grid variant: set role="grid" on the table, move the selection to aria-selected="true" on the day's td in place of aria-pressed, and give every day tabindex="-1" except one, which is the selected day, or else today, or else the first day that can be chosen. Left and Right move focus one day, Up and Down one week, Home and End to the start and the end of the week, Page Up and Page Down one month, and Shift with Page Up or Page Down one year. Moving past either end of the month shows the next month and keeps focus on the day reached. A day that cannot be chosen takes aria-disabled="true" in place of disabled, so the arrows can cross it, and the app ignores presses on it. Enter and Space choose the focused day.
When the calendar is in a popover or a sheet, choosing a day closes it and returns focus to the control that opened it. Escape closes it and changes nothing.

components.name: check-list
components.title: Check list
components.purpose: The results of the automated checks on a run: each check's name, its result in words, how long it took and, behind a disclosure, its output.
whenToUse: As the evidence for a run or a pull request: lint, type check, tests and build, each with its result.
Where the reader decides whether to approve work and needs to see what was verified and what failed.
whenNotToUse: For the steps a run took, in the order they happened. Use the timeline or the activity feed.
For one check or one overall status. Write it as a badge or a sentence.
For a list of tasks the reader ticks off. Use checkboxes.
For results compared across runs. Use the data table.

variants.name: passed
variants.use: The check ran and passed. The word is Passed, beside a check mark in a circle.

variants.name: failed
variants.use: The check ran and failed. The word is Failed, or says how much failed, beside an alert mark. Its row holds the output.

variants.name: running
variants.use: The check has started and not finished. The word is Running, beside a turning mark.

variants.name: skipped
variants.use: The check did not run and will not. The words say Skipped and why, beside a barred circle.

variants.name: not started
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The check is waiting for its turn. The words are Not started, beside three dots.

accessibility: Use a ul with the class gw-check-list__items and one li with gw-check-list__item for each check, inside a div with gw-check-list. A screen reader then says how many checks there are.

Start with gw-check-list__summary, a p that counts in words: 7 of 12 checks passed, then how many failed, are running and were skipped. Give it role="status" when results arrive while the reader watches, so the new count is announced.

Each row holds, in this order, gw-check-list__name, gw-check-list__result and gw-check-list__duration, all spans. The result is always a word, Passed, Failed, Running, Skipped or Not started, and the stylesheet draws its icon from the modifier class, so no result is an icon or a colour alone.

Write the duration with its unit inside a time element with a datetime duration: 1 min 48 s. A check that has not finished or did not run has an empty gw-check-list__duration, or says what it waits for.

Output goes in a details element with gw-check-list__output after the three spans. Its summary, gw-check-list__toggle, has text that names the check: Output, with the check's name in a gw-visually-hidden span. The pre with gw-check-list__log holds the output as text and wraps, so it never scrolls sideways.
A failed check's output starts closed unless the view is about that failure. Trim it to the lines that explain the failure and link to the full log.
Put failed checks first, then running, then passed and skipped, so what needs the reader is at the top.
Tab reaches each summary, and Enter and Space open and close it. The component needs no script.
While the results are fetched, show a spinner with its text in place of the list. If they cannot be read, show an error state. If no checks are set up, show an empty state that says so.

components.name: checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.purpose: A native checkbox with its label: one yes-or-no choice, or several independent choices in a group, sent with a form.
whenToUse: For a choice the reader confirms with the rest of a form, such as Open the pull request as a draft.
For several options where any number may be chosen, in a fieldset with a legend.
For a select-all box over a list, which is indeterminate while only some rows are selected.
whenNotToUse: For a setting that takes effect the moment it changes. Use a switch.
To choose exactly one of several options. Use a radio group, or a segmented control for two to five short options.
To choose one of many options. Use a select.

variants.name: single
variants.use: The default: a div with gw-checkbox holding the input, the label, and optionally a description and an error.

variants.name: group
variants.use: A fieldset holding a gw-checkbox__legend and one gw-checkbox per option, one above the other.

accessibility: Use input type="checkbox" with gw-checkbox__input, followed by a label with gw-checkbox__label whose for attribute is the input's id. The input comes first in the markup: the stylesheet reads its state to style the label after it.
A description is a p with gw-checkbox__description, linked from the input with aria-describedby.
Group related checkboxes in a fieldset with gw-checkbox__group, and name the group with a legend carrying gw-checkbox__legend.

Indeterminate cannot be written in markup. The app sets the property with script, input.indeterminate = true, and clears it when the box is next changed. A screen reader then announces it as mixed. Do not set aria-checked on a native checkbox.
For an error, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a p with gw-checkbox__error through aria-describedby. The message says what to do, and its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Set the disabled attribute when the choice is unavailable, and say why in the description. A disabled checkbox leaves the tab order.
Tab reaches each checkbox and Space toggles it. The box is drawn 20px square and its pointer target is 44px; a press on the label toggles it too.

components.name: code-block
components.title: Code block
components.purpose: A block of mono text for a command, a log or a program's output.
whenToUse: For a command the reader may copy, the output of a command, a log, or an excerpt of a file.
With the scroll variant when columns must stay aligned, such as a table printed by a tool.
With line numbers when the text refers to lines of a file.
whenNotToUse: For a change to a file. Use the diff.
For a word or a path inside a sentence. Use a code element in the running text.
For a value the reader edits. Use a field.
For prose, or to make a message look technical. Mono text is for text a machine wrote or will read.

variants.name: wrapping
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Long lines wrap at any character, so nothing is hidden at phone width.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: Lines keep their length and the body scrolls sideways inside the block. Set tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label on the body.

With the scroll variant, give the pre tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label that says what it holds. It can then take focus, and the arrow keys scroll it. Leave all three off a wrapping block, which never scrolls.

For line numbers, give the code element the class gw-code-block__lines and write each line as a gw-code-block__line span holding a gw-code-block__number span and a gw-code-block__text span. The numbers are real text, so a screen reader reads them, and they are left out of a copy.
Write the text exactly as the tool printed it. Escape the characters <, > and & in markup.
When there is no output, keep the caption and replace the pre with a gw-code-block__note paragraph that says so in a sentence. Never show an empty box.
Colour carries no meaning inside a block. A failure is said in the output's own words or in text beside the block.

components.name: combobox
components.title: Combobox
components.purpose: A text input that filters a list of options as the reader types, for one choice from a list too long to scan.
whenToUse: For one choice from a long list the reader can name: a branch, a repository, a teammate, a model.
When typing a few characters is faster than scrolling, from about fifteen options up.
whenNotToUse: For a short fixed list. Use a select, which opens the picker each platform already has.
To filter a list the reader can already see on the page. Use a search field.
For several values at once. Use a tag input.
For a menu of actions. Use a menu.
For free text with no list behind it. Use a field.

variants.name: plain
variants.use: The input, the panel and the status line inside gw-combobox.

variants.name: with a leading icon
variants.use: An svg with gw-combobox__icon before the input, to say what kind of thing is chosen. No modifier class is needed.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The input is 44px tall and as wide as the field. Each option is at least 44px tall, and the panel scrolls after five and a half options.

accessibility: Inside gw-field, after the label, put an element with gw-combobox. Use the gw-combobox element when the page loads behaviors/combobox.js, and a div when a framework sets the attributes itself. The styles are the same for both.

The input carries gw-field__control and gw-combobox__input, with type="text", role="combobox", aria-autocomplete="list", autocomplete="off", aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the list's id. Its label is the field's label element.

After the input comes a div with gw-combobox__panel. It holds a ul with gw-combobox__list, role="listbox", an id and an aria-label, then a p with gw-combobox__message and the hidden attribute. Each option is an li with gw-combobox__option, role="option", an id and aria-selected.

Open is aria-expanded="true" on the input. The active option is the one with aria-selected="true", and the input's aria-activedescendant holds its id, so focus never leaves the input. An option that does not match carries the hidden attribute. No class marks any of this.

The last child is a p with role="status" and gw-visually-hidden. After each change to what is typed, write the count into it with its unit, such as 2 of 41 branches, so a screen reader announces it. With the gw-combobox element, give it data-gw-count holding the sentence with {count} and {total}, and the element writes it.

When nothing matches, set aria-expanded="false", set hidden on the list, remove hidden from the message and copy its text into the status line. The message says that nothing matches and what to try. The same message element says what is being fetched while options load.

Keys, which the gw-combobox element provides: typing filters and opens the list. Down and Up open it and move the active option, wrapping at the ends. Home and End go to the first and last option while the list is open. Enter chooses the active option, writes its text into the input, closes the list and sends a change event. Escape closes the list and keeps what was typed. A press on an option chooses it. Leaving the input closes the list.
An option's value is its text. Put a different value to write into the input in data-value on the option.
The element matches the typed text anywhere in an option, ignoring case. An app that fetches options from a server filters them itself and sets the same attributes.
For a value that is not in the list, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that says to choose from the list.
The chevron is decoration drawn by the stylesheet. The leading icon carries aria-hidden="true".

The input says it is a combobox and whether its list is open, the active option is named through aria-activedescendant, and the count is announced, so the keyboard and a screen reader get everything the pointer gets.

components.name: command-palette
components.title: Command palette
components.purpose: A modal dialog with a search input over a grouped list of commands, for running any command of the app from the keyboard.
whenToUse: As a second, faster way to run the commands of the app, opened from a button and from a keyboard shortcut such as Ctrl or Cmd with K.
When the app has more commands than its views can show as buttons, and the reader knows the name of what they want.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to run a command. Every command is also a button or a menu item in the view it belongs to.
For the actions on one item. Use a menu, or the context menu on a row.
To search content, such as runs or files. Use a search field above the list it filters.
To choose a value in a form. Use a select or a listbox.

variants.name: grouped
variants.use: The default. Commands sit in gw-command-palette__group elements under a gw-command-palette__label that names their subject.

variants.name: flat
variants.use: For a handful of commands on one subject, the options sit straight inside the list with no group.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The width of the dialog, 480px at most. The list shows about eight commands and then scrolls.

accessibility: The palette is the dialog component: a dialog element with gw-dialog and an aria-label, opened with showModal(), which traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to what opened it. The examples carry the open attribute only so the gallery draws them. Inside it is one div with gw-command-palette.

gw-command-palette__search holds the search field's markup with gw-command-palette__field added, and a form with method="dialog" holding an icon button named Close the command palette, because a touch screen has no Escape key. The label of the input is visually hidden, never missing.

The input is type="text" with role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at the list, aria-autocomplete="list" and aria-activedescendant holding the id of the command Enter would run. Focus never leaves the input while the reader types and moves.

The list is a div with gw-command-palette__list, role="listbox" and an aria-label. A group is a div with gw-command-palette__group, role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-command-palette__label, which carries role="presentation".

Each command is a button with type="button", gw-command-palette__option, role="option", an id and aria-selected. It holds an optional icon with aria-hidden="true", its name in a span with gw-command-palette__name, a verb and what it acts on, and optionally a kbd with gw-command-palette__shortcut. Because it is a button, a press runs it and, with no script, Tab reaches it and Enter runs it.
A command that cannot run now carries aria-disabled="true" and says why in its name. It stays in the arrow-key order, and neither Enter nor a press runs it.

The message is a p with gw-command-palette__message, role="status" and the hidden attribute. When nothing matches it is shown, the list is hidden and aria-expanded is "false". It says what to try. While commands load, a div with gw-command-palette__message holds a spinner with its text in place of the list.

The behaviour is script. Wrap the dialog in the gw-command-palette element from behaviors/command-palette.js, or set the same attributes from a framework: typing hides the options and the groups that do not match by setting hidden on them, Down and Up move aria-selected="true" and aria-activedescendant through the options that are shown and wrap at the ends, and Enter presses the selected option. A press on an option closes the dialog after the app's own click listener has run.

The element's shortcut attribute names one key: shortcut="k" opens the dialog on Ctrl with K and on Cmd with K. Say so on the opener with aria-keyshortcuts="Control+K Meta+K". Closing the dialog empties the input, so the palette opens on the full list.
The opener is a button that calls showModal() on the dialog, or carries command="show-modal" and commandfor with the dialog's id where invoker commands are supported.

components.name: composer
components.title: Composer
components.purpose: The prompt input under a transcript: a textarea that grows with its content, and Send.
whenToUse: At the bottom of a transcript, to send the next prompt to the agent.
To stop a running turn from the same place the reader sends from.
whenNotToUse: For one line of text in a form, such as a task title. Use a field.
For longer text that is saved with a form and not sent as a message. Use a textarea.
To answer an approval request. Use the approval's own Allow and Decline.

variants.name: default
variants.use: In the flow of the page, as wide as its container.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Held to the bottom of the scrolling view, with a top border, its own padding and room for the home indicator. Make the view's scroller end at the visible viewport, with a height in dvh or interactive-widget=resizes-content in the viewport meta tag, so it stays above an on-screen keyboard.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The textarea is one line and 44px tall when empty and grows with its content to 176px, then scrolls. Where field-sizing is not supported it is a fixed 88px. Send stays beside the last line.

accessibility: Use a form element, so Send submits it. The textarea has a visible gw-composer__label whose for attribute matches its id, or an aria-label when the view has no room for one. A placeholder is not a label.
Send is a button of type submit with gw-button gw-button--primary. It is the view's one primary action, so nothing else in the view is primary.

While a turn runs, the app sets aria-busy="true" on the form and replaces Send with a Stop button of type button and secondary emphasis. Never show both. The textarea stays editable, and a line of gw-composer__reason linked by aria-describedby says when sending is possible again.
When the reader cannot send, set disabled on the textarea and on Send, and say why in gw-composer__reason, linked from both by aria-describedby. The reason says what to do next.
When a prompt fails to send, keep the text in the textarea and add gw-composer__error with role="alert", linked by aria-describedby. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Tab moves from the textarea to Send, then to the quiet controls. The app decides whether Enter sends. If it does, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the button remains the way to send on a phone.
The component needs no script. The app sets disabled, aria-busy and aria-describedby, and swaps Send for Stop.

components.name: confirm-dialog
components.title: Confirm dialog
components.purpose: A dialog that asks before something is deleted or discarded, and says in plain words what will be lost.
whenToUse: Before an action the reader started that deletes or discards something and cannot be undone, such as deleting a workspace or discarding a draft.
whenNotToUse: For an action that can be reversed. Do it at once and show an undo toast.
For a request from an agent that waits for an answer. Use an approval.
For a task with fields to fill in. Use a dialog.
To confirm an ordinary action such as saving. Do not ask.
accessibility: Use the dialog markup with both classes on the dialog element, gw-dialog and gw-confirm-dialog, and add role="alertdialog". A screen reader then reads the question and its description at once, where a plain dialog would read only the title.
Point aria-labelledby at the title and aria-describedby at gw-dialog__body, so the list of what is lost is part of what is read.

The title names the thing: Delete the workspace api-refactor? The body says what will be lost, one thing per gw-confirm-dialog__loss, and that it cannot be undone. Say what is kept when the reader might fear for it.

Cancel is the first button and the destructive button the second. Open with showModal(), which moves focus to the first button, so focus starts on Cancel. Never put autofocus on the destructive button.
The destructive button is gw-button gw-button--danger and repeats the verb and the thing: Delete workspace. It is never gw-button--primary, and a confirm dialog has no primary button.
The footer carries gw-dialog__footer and gw-confirm-dialog__actions, which holds Cancel at the start and the destructive button at the far end.
Escape cancels. Both buttons close the dialog through the form with method="dialog", and the app deletes only when dialog.returnValue is the destructive button's value.

While deleting, set aria-busy="true" on the destructive button, change its label and disable Cancel. If it fails, keep the dialog open and put an alert with role="alert" at the top of the body saying that nothing was deleted and what to do.

components.name: context-menu
components.title: Context menu
components.purpose: The actions on one row of a list or a table, in a menu opened from a More actions button at the end of the row.
whenToUse: When each row of a list or a table has three or more actions and no room to show them.
Where the app also wants a right-click or a long press on the row to open the same menu.
whenNotToUse: For one action per row. Show it as a small quiet button in the row.
For the actions of the whole view. Use a menu opened from a labelled button, or a toolbar.
For a menu that opens only on a right-click or a long press. A phone has no right-click and neither can be found: always give the row its button.
For an action the reader must not miss, such as answering an approval. Show it in the row.
accessibility: Wrap the button and the menu in a div with the class gw-context-menu, the menu straight after the button. Add gw-context-menu__button to the button and gw-context-menu__menu to the menu, beside the classes of the icon button and the menu. In a list row the wrapper sits in gw-list__action, and in a table in the row's last cell.

The button is an icon button with the ellipsis icon, popovertarget with the menu's id, aria-haspopup="menu" and a name that includes the row, such as More actions for run 4182. In a list of rows that all end in this button, the name is what tells them apart.

The browser opens and closes the menu from the button, sets aria-expanded, closes on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the button. While the menu is open its button is drawn with a border and a fill, so the reader can tell which row it acts on.

A right-click and a long press are the app's to add, and only as a second way in. On the row's contextmenu event, which a long press also fires on most touch screens, call preventDefault() and then showPopover({ source: button }) on the menu, so it opens in the same place with the same items.
Every action in the menu is reachable from the button. Never add an item, or a whole menu, that only a right-click or a long press can reach.

The keyboard inside the menu is the menu component's contract: Tab and Enter with no script, and arrow keys where the app adds them. Shift with F10 and the Menu key fire the contextmenu event on the focused row link in most browsers, and so open the menu too once the app handles that event.
The item that deletes is last, below a divider, with gw-menu__item--danger, and names the row.

components.title: Copy button
components.purpose: A small button that copies a value shown next to it, and says in words that it did.
whenToUse: Beside a value the view already shows as text, where the reader may want it on the clipboard: a branch name in a row, a commit hash in a key-value list, a command in a table cell.
Above a block of code or a log, to copy the whole block.
With only an icon where several values in a dense list each have one.
whenNotToUse: When taking the value away is the point of the view, such as a clone URL or a token shown once. Use the copy field, which puts the value in a box that can be selected and scrolled.
For a value the view does not show. The reader must be able to see what will be copied.
For a secret. Do not put one on the clipboard from a button in a list.
For any action other than copying. Use a button.

variants.name: with a label
variants.use: The default: gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small with the copy icon and the word Copy.

variants.name: icon only
variants.use: gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-icon-button with the copy icon and an aria-label, for a dense row or a table cell. It is 44px square.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The labelled button is drawn 32px tall with a 44px pointer target. The icon-only button is 44px square.

accessibility: Wrap the button and its status in a span with the class gw-copy-button. The button is a gw-button with type="button"; this component adds no class to it.
Give the button an aria-label that starts with Copy and names the value, such as Copy branch name, so several on one view can be told apart. The icon carries aria-hidden="true".
Keep an empty span with gw-copy-button__status and role="status" next to the button from the start, after it or, at the trailing end of a row, before it. role="status" is a polite live region.

The app copies with navigator.clipboard.writeText() on a press, then sets the status text to Copied, or to what was copied, such as Branch name copied. A screen reader announces it and sighted readers see the same word. Clear the text after about 2 seconds.
The confirmation is that word. Do not signal a copy by changing the button's colour or icon alone, do not change the button's name, and do not move focus away from the button.
If the copy fails, set the status text to say so and what to do: Not copied. Select the text and copy it by hand.
Set the disabled attribute while there is nothing to copy yet.
Tab reaches the button, and Enter and Space press it. Both come from the button element.

whenNotToUse: For a value the reader can change. Use a text input in a field.

components.name: data-table
components.title: Data table
components.purpose: Things compared across columns on a real table: a caption, sortable headers, numeric columns, one action for each row, rows that expand, and a stacked layout on a phone.
whenToUse: When the reader compares the same facts across several things: runs by duration and tokens, repositories by usage, branches by age.
With the default stacked layout when each row can be read by itself on a phone: below 768px a row becomes a block and each cell prints its column label beside its value.
With the scroll variant when the reader compares down a column even on a phone, or when the headers sort: the columns stay and the table scrolls sideways inside its wrapper.
With the sticky variant for a table long enough that the header would scroll out of sight.
whenNotToUse: For things the reader scans and opens, with one or two facts each. Use the list.
For the facts of one thing. Use the key-value list.
For layout. A table is for data with column headers.
For a sortable table in the stacked layout. The header row is not drawn below 768px, so its buttons would be out of reach: use the scroll variant, or offer the order in a select above the table.
For a row with two or more actions. Open the row's own view, or put the rest in its detail row.
For a table nested in a table's detail row. Put facts there as text or a key-value list.

variants.name: stacked
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Columns at 768px and wider. Below that each row is a block: its th is the block's title and each td prints the label in its data-label attribute beside its value. The header row is not drawn.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: Columns at every width. Put the table inside a div with the class gw-data-table__scroll, which scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit. Cells do not wrap.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: The header row stays at the top of whatever scrolls the table up and down, on the page surface. It has no effect inside gw-data-table__scroll unless the app gives that wrapper a height, and none in the stacked layout below 768px.

accessibility: Use a table with a caption, gw-data-table__caption, that says what the rows are. Column headers are th scope="col" in a thead, and the cell that names each row is a th scope="row". Do not build a table from divs.

Give every td a data-label attribute holding the text of its column header. Below 768px the stylesheet prints it beside the value, and it is read out with the value. Leave it off the action cell, a detail cell and a state cell.
A cell holds one run of text or one element. In the stacked layout a second element would start a new line under the label.
A column of numbers carries gw-data-table__numeric on its th and on every td: right-aligned, in tabular figures, each number with its unit.

A sortable header is a button with the class gw-data-table__sort inside the th, holding the header's words. Set aria-sort="ascending" or aria-sort="descending" on the th of the one column the rows are ordered by, and leave it off the others. The stylesheet draws the direction from that attribute. The app reorders the rows and moves the attribute, and the caption or a role="status" line says the new order.

A row has at most one action: a small quiet button in a td with the class gw-data-table__action, the last cell of the row, under a th whose text is in a gw-visually-hidden span. When every row's button has the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the row. The cell pads the 32px button out to 44px, so its pointer target fits the row and a one-line row is no taller.

A row that expands has a button with the class gw-data-table__expand in its th, holding the words that name the row, with aria-expanded and with aria-controls pointing at the next row. That next row is a tr with the class gw-data-table__detail holding one td that spans every column. The app sets aria-expanded to true or false and nothing else: the stylesheet does not draw the detail row while the button says false. Do not use the hidden attribute on the detail row.
Mark the selected row with aria-selected="true" on its tr. It is drawn with a bar at its start as well as a shade.

With no rows, while loading and after a failure, keep the caption and the header and put one row in the tbody whose single td has the class gw-data-table__state and spans every column. Empty: a gw-data-table__message sentence saying why, and at most one small button. Loading: a spinner with role="status", and aria-busy="true" on the table. Error: a gw-data-table__message with role="alert" that says what to do, and a small Retry button. The stylesheet draws the failure's icon.
A status in a cell is written in words. One badge may hold it.

The wrapper of the scroll variant carries tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-labelledby pointing at the caption's id, so a keyboard can scroll it with the arrow keys. Give each such table on a view a different caption.
Tab moves through the header buttons, then each row's expand button and action, in order. Enter and Space activate them. There are no arrow-key bindings between cells.

The numbers are right-aligned in tabular figures with their units, and on a phone each row becomes a block whose cells print their column label from data-label.

components.name: date-field
components.title: Date field
components.purpose: A native date input, or date and time input, as the control of a field, with a hint for what to enter and its earliest and latest values.
whenToUse: For one calendar day the reader knows or picks: an expiry date, the start of a filter.
With type="datetime-local", for a day and a time together, such as when a scheduled run starts.
whenNotToUse: For a date the reader knows by heart and that is far in the past, such as a date of birth. Use three fields: day, month and year.
For a rough span of time, such as the last 7 days. Use a select or a segmented control of ready-made ranges.
For a length of time, such as 30 minutes. Use a number field with a unit.
To show a date the reader cannot change and will not send with a form. Write it as plain text, such as 14 March 2026.

variants.name: date
variants.use: input type="date". At most 220px wide.

variants.name: date and time
variants.use: input type="datetime-local". At most 286px wide. Set step, in seconds, to limit the minutes it offers.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. The calendar button inside it is the browser's own, with a widened pointer target.

accessibility: Use input type="date" or type="datetime-local" carrying gw-field__control and gw-date-field, inside gw-field. The label, description and error are the field's. There is no wrapper and no custom calendar.
The value, min and max are always written as 2026-11-22, or 2026-11-22T09:30 with a time, whatever the reader sees. The browser shows and reads the date in the reader's own format.

Because that format and the order of its parts differ from reader to reader, the hint never spells a pattern such as DD/MM/YYYY. The description gives the earliest and latest day with the month as a word, such as Any day from 24 August to 22 November 2026, which also shows the reader what a full date holds. For a time, it names the time zone.
Set min and max to the same range the description gives, and check the value on the server as well: a browser may let the reader type a day outside the range.
For a day out of range, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that names the limit and says what to choose.
The keyboard is the browser's own: Tab moves between the day, month and year, the arrow keys change each, typing digits fills it, and in most browsers Space, or Alt and Down, opens the calendar.
An empty input shows the browser's own outline of the format. Do not add a placeholder.
A read-only date stays focusable and can be read. A disabled one leaves the tab order, and its description says how to make it available.

components.name: device-code
components.title: Device code
components.purpose: What a view shows while the reader connects an outside account by entering a short code on that account's own site: the steps, the link, the code, and whether the app is still waiting.
whenToUse: To connect GitHub or another account with the device authorisation flow, where the reader opens the provider's page, on this device or another, and types a code the app shows.
Inside a sheet's body opened from a Connect button, or straight on a setup page.
whenNotToUse: When the provider can send the reader back to the app by itself. Use a button that starts that sign-in.
For a token or a key the reader pastes into the app. Use a field.
For a value to copy that is not a one-time code, such as a clone URL. Use the copy field.
For a code the app sends to the reader's phone or email to type back in. Use a field with autocomplete="one-time-code".
accessibility: Use a div with gw-device-code. The steps are an ol with gw-device-code__steps, one li with gw-device-code__step for each, in plain words: open the page, enter the code, approve and come back. The stylesheet draws the numbers and a screen reader announces them from the ol.

The verification address is a real link whose text shows the host and path, such as github.com/login/device, so the reader can check where the code is going before they follow it. It opens in a new tab so this view keeps waiting, and says so in a gw-link__hint.

The code is a p with gw-device-code__code inside gw-device-code__entry. For the eye it is split into spans with gw-device-code__group, with the provider's separator between them, inside a span with aria-hidden="true". For a screen reader it is one string, exactly as the provider issued it, in a gw-visually-hidden span before that: Code: WDJB-MJHT. Never give the code only as an image.
The Copy control is the copy button: a gw-button named Copy code, with its gw-copy-button__status beside it. It copies the code exactly as issued, and the app writes Code copied into the status.

gw-device-code__status holds the waiting line, a p with gw-spinner and role="status", and a p with gw-device-code__note that says when the code expires as a time of day. A screen reader hears the waiting line once. Do not announce a countdown.

The app polls the provider. When the account is connected it replaces the steps and the status with a success alert that has role="status", says which account was connected, and offers the one way on.

When the code expires, write the visible code in an s element in place of the aria-hidden span, which strikes it through, add the word expired to the string for screen readers, disable Copy code, and replace the waiting line with a warning alert that has role="alert", says the code can no longer be used and offers Get a new code. A new code replaces the old one in place, and the app says so in the waiting line.
When the reader declines at the provider, or the provider cannot be reached, show a danger alert with role="alert" that says which of the two happened, that nothing was connected, and what to do.
Tab reaches the link, Copy code and then whatever follows in the sheet or the page. The component has no keys of its own and needs no script beyond the polling and the copy.

components.name: dialog
components.title: Dialog
components.purpose: A modal window for one short task that must be finished or cancelled before the reader goes on.
whenToUse: For a short task the reader starts from the current view and finishes in one step, such as renaming a branch.
To ask a question the view cannot go on without, with one primary action and Cancel.
whenNotToUse: To confirm deleting or discarding something. Use the confirm dialog.
For a longer form, filters or the details of an item. Use a sheet.
For supplementary content beside a control that should not block the page. Use a popover.
To report that something happened. Use a toast, or an alert for a result that stays.

variants.name: default
variants.use: No modifier class. The dialog grows with its content and scrolls as a whole once it reaches the height of the screen.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: A body that may be long, such as a list of files. The title and the footer stay in place and the body scrolls between two rules.

accessibility: Use a dialog element with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-dialog__title, an h2. When the body is one short text, point aria-describedby at it.

Open it with the one line document.getElementById("dialog-id").showModal(). That call traps focus, makes the page behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener when the dialog closes. Do not write the open attribute yourself, which shows the dialog without any of that: the examples carry it only so they are drawn in the gallery.

As progressive enhancement, the opener may carry command="show-modal" and commandfor="dialog-id", and then needs no script where invoker commands are supported. Keep the showModal() call for browsers without them.

Wrap the content in a form with method="dialog" and the class gw-dialog__panel. Each footer button is a submit button with a value. Pressing one closes the dialog with no script, and the app reads dialog.returnValue in a close event listener. To validate or save before closing, handle the form's submit event and call preventDefault().
The primary button comes first in the footer and Cancel second, so Enter in a field takes the primary action. Cancel carries formnovalidate so it closes a form with an empty required field.
showModal() moves focus to the first focusable element, or to the one that has the autofocus attribute. Tab stays inside the dialog.
A dialog has one primary button. It is a view of its own, so the page behind may have its own.
With gw-dialog--scroll, if the body holds no control, give gw-dialog__body tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label so the keyboard can scroll it.

While saving, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button, change its label to say what is happening and disable Cancel. If it fails, keep the dialog open and say what happened and what to do, in the field's error or in an alert inside the body.

For a change to prose that the reader edits in place. Show the text itself.
accessibility: Use a figure. Its figcaption, gw-diff__header, holds the path in a code element and the counts. Leave the header out when the diff sits under a summary that already shows both.
Write each count as a sign and a number followed by a gw-diff__label span that finishes it in words, such as +7 and lines added. The label is hidden from sight and read by a screen reader.
The body is a pre with tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label naming the file, so it can take focus and the arrow keys scroll it sideways. The page itself never scrolls sideways.

Each line is a gw-diff__line holding a gw-diff__sign cell and a gw-diff__text cell. Use an ins element for an added line and a del element for a removed one, with the plus or minus as the sign. A context line and a hunk header are spans, with a space as the sign.
Never leave out the sign. The shading alone does not mark a line for someone who cannot tell the colours apart.

While the diff is fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the figure and put a gw-diff__note with role="status" in place of the body. When it fails, use a note with role="alert" that says why. The stylesheet adds the failure's icon.
When a file changed with no line to show, or the diff is cut short, say so in a plain gw-diff__note.

components.name: disclosure
components.title: Disclosure
components.purpose: A native details element that shows or hides detail under a summary written in text.
whenToUse: For detail most readers can do without: a log, the environment, the steps of a finished attempt.
With the row variant inside a list row, for a changed file that opens to its diff. The summary holds the path and the counts.
For the one group of advanced settings in a view. Mark that details element with data-gw-advanced.
whenNotToUse: For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical that can be reached only inside closed content fails the hidden-critical-action rule: show it in the view too, or open the disclosure by default.
Nested more than two levels. A third level fails the disclosure-depth rule: move that content to a view of its own.
With a summary that is only an icon or is empty. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule.
For a list of actions that opens over the page. Use a menu.
For sections where opening one must close the others. This component has no script, so each disclosure opens and closes alone.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Stands alone. Its content is indented to start under the summary's text.

variants.name: row
variants.use: The only child of a gw-list__row. The summary is the row, and the content uses the row's full width, which a diff needs at phone width.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The summary is at least 44px tall and as wide as the disclosure. It grows when its text wraps.

accessibility: Use a details element with a summary as its first child. The browser gives the summary its role and its expanded state, and the open attribute is the only state: never toggle a class.
The summary holds text that says what is inside. The chevron is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup. Do not put a heading, a button or a link inside the summary.

Trailing text such as a count goes in a gw-disclosure__meta span inside the summary, after the label. It is read as part of the summary's name, so write counts in words or with a hidden label, as gw-diff__counts does.
Put the content in one gw-disclosure__content element after the summary.

Tab reaches the summary. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order and is skipped by a screen reader, and the browser's find-in-page opens it.
Set the open attribute in markup to start open. Start open when the content holds an action the reader needs.
Fetch heavy content, such as a diff, when the disclosure opens, and show the content's own loading state until it arrives.

components.name: editable-list
components.title: Editable list
components.purpose: An ordered list whose items the reader can edit in place, add to and delete from, such as the tasks in an agent's plan before it is approved.
whenToUse: For a short ordered list of one-line items the reader corrects before something acts on it: the tasks of a plan, the setup commands of a repository.
When each item is one line of text and every change is small enough to make in the row.
whenNotToUse: To change the order of the items. This component has no reordering: no drag handle and no move buttons. If order must change, the app needs its own control, and until then the reader deletes an item and adds it again at the end.
For items with more than one field. Make each row a link to a view or a sheet that edits it.
For a list the reader only reads or opens. Use the list.
For rows compared across columns. Use the data table.
For tasks the reader ticks off. Use checkboxes.
accessibility: Use an ol with the class gw-editable-list__items and an aria-label that names the list, inside a div with gw-editable-list. Each item is an li with gw-editable-list__item. The stylesheet draws each item's number from its place in the list, and a screen reader announces the position from the ol.

A row at rest holds a span with gw-editable-list__text and a span with gw-editable-list__actions holding two buttons, Edit then Delete, each gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small. They are drawn 32px tall and their pointer targets are 44px. Row actions are never primary.
Each button's aria-label starts with its visible word and names the row: Edit task 2: Raise the session timeout to 30 minutes.

Editing: the app replaces the row's text and buttons with a form with gw-editable-list__editor. It holds a gw-field whose visible label names the item, such as Task 2, with the item's text as the input's value, then gw-editable-list__editor-actions with a submit button, Save task, and a quiet Cancel. Move focus to the input. Only one row is edited at a time.
Enter in the input saves, because it submits the form. The app also cancels on Escape. After Save or Cancel the row goes back to rest and focus returns to its Edit button.

An empty item is not saved. Set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that says what to do. While the save is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the submit button, change its words to Saving task, make the input readonly and disable Cancel. If the save fails, keep the row in editing with the reader's text and say so in a gw-field__error with role="alert".

Adding: gw-editable-list__add after the ol holds one quiet button with a plus icon, Add task. Pressing it appends a row in the editing state with an empty input labelled New task and hides the Add button until that row is saved or cancelled.

Deleting: Delete removes the row at once, with no question first, and the app shows the undo toast, Done: Task 3 deleted from the plan, with Undo for at least 10 seconds. Move focus to the Edit button of the row that took its place, or to Add task when it was the last. Undo puts the item back in its old position and moves focus to its Edit button.
The order of the items is fixed. Tab moves through each row's Edit and Delete and then Add task. There are no arrow-key bindings.

When the list cannot be changed, such as after the plan is approved, disable every button and say why in a p with gw-editable-list__note before the list. When there are no items, show an empty state in place of the ol and keep Add task.

whenToUse: In place of a list, table or panel that has nothing in it yet.

With the compact size, for an empty section inside a list or a panel.

components.name: feedback
components.title: Feedback
components.purpose: A control for rating an agent's answer as helpful or not helpful, with an optional follow-up note and a confirmation.
whenToUse: Under an agent's answer or at the end of a turn, to record whether it helped.
When a rating can be followed by an optional note on what was wrong.
whenNotToUse: To answer a request an agent is waiting on. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
To accept or reject a run's work. Use buttons that name the action, such as Accept changes.
For a rating on a scale, or a choice among several options. Use radio inputs in a field.
For a setting that turns something on or off. Use a checkbox or a switch.
accessibility: Use a div with role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at gw-feedback__prompt, which asks the question in words, such as Was this answer helpful?

Each choice is a button element with type="button" and the classes gw-button gw-button--small gw-feedback__choice, and the two sit together in gw-feedback__choices. It holds an icon with aria-hidden="true" and the words Helpful or Not helpful. Never use the icon alone.

Both buttons carry aria-pressed. The app sets aria-pressed="true" on the chosen one and "false" on the other. Pressing the chosen button again clears the rating. The pressed button is drawn with a darker outline, a shade and a heavier label, not a colour alone.

Keep an empty p with the class gw-feedback__confirmation and role="status" in the group from the start. After a choice is saved, the app writes one line into it, such as Rated helpful. Thank you., and a screen reader announces it. It takes no room while empty.

The follow-up note is an app-set pattern, not a state of the component. After a choice, the app inserts gw-feedback__note between the row and the confirmation, or removes its hidden attribute: a gw-field whose control is a gw-textarea, with a visible label, and a secondary button, Send note. The rating is saved by the first press, and the note is optional. Do not move focus into the field: the reader reaches it with Tab.
After the note is sent, set the disabled attribute on both choices, leave aria-pressed as it is, remove the note field and say so in the confirmation.

If saving fails, set both buttons back to aria-pressed="false" and add a p with the class gw-feedback__error and role="alert" that says the rating was not saved and what to do. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Tab reaches Helpful, then Not helpful, then the note field and Send note when shown. Enter and Space press a button. The buttons are drawn 32px tall with a 44px pointer target.

components.name: file-upload
components.title: File upload
components.purpose: A file input drawn as a drop area with a button in it, with what it accepts in words and the chosen files listed under it.
whenToUse: In a form, to send one or more files from the reader's device: logs and screenshots for a task, an environment file for a workspace.
When the reader should see what is accepted before choosing, and each file's progress and failure after.
whenNotToUse: To attach a file to a prompt. Use the composer's attach button, with attachment chips above it.
To point at a file that is already in the repository. Use a field for its path, or a combobox.
To paste text. Use a textarea.

variants.use: No multiple attribute, and the prompt reads Choose a file, or drop it here. A new file replaces the one chosen.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: As wide as the field and at least 88px tall. The whole area is the pointer target.

accessibility: Inside gw-field, after the label, put a div with gw-file-upload. It holds an input type="file" with gw-file-upload__input, then a div with gw-file-upload__prompt and aria-hidden="true". The label's for attribute matches the input's id, so a screen reader hears the label and the browser's own file button.

The prompt is what sighted readers see in place of the browser's button: a span with gw-button and gw-file-upload__button, such as Choose files, and a span of plain words, such as or drop them here. It is a picture of the input, not a second control, so it is hidden from assistive technology and takes no pointer events.
The input covers the whole area. A press or a drop anywhere on it reaches the input itself, so choosing and dropping both work with no script, and Tab, Enter and Space are the browser's own.

Say what is accepted in words in a gw-field__description linked with aria-describedby: the kinds of file, how many, and the size limit with its unit. Set accept on the input to the same kinds. Check type and size again on the server.

Dragover is the one state the app sets: add the data-dragover attribute to the gw-file-upload element on dragenter and dragover, and remove it on dragleave and drop. The border turns solid and the area is shaded. The app may also change the prompt's words, such as Drop to add 2 files.

List the chosen files under the description in a ul with gw-cluster, gw-gap-md and gw-file-upload__files and an aria-label such as Files chosen. Each file is an attachment chip, copied from that component: its name, its size in words and a remove button that names the file.

While files upload, each chip carries aria-busy="true" and a progress element, as the attachment chip describes, and the description, with role="status", says how many are done. The reader can still add files.

A file that cannot be added at all has no chip: set aria-invalid="true" on the input and add a gw-field__error with role="alert" that names the file, says why and says what to add. A file that was added and then failed keeps its chip, with the chip's own error. Remove aria-invalid when the reader next chooses a file.
After a file is removed, move focus to the next chip's remove button, or to the input when none is left.
Set the disabled attribute on the input when no more files can be added, and say why in the description.

components.name: filter-chips
components.title: Filter chips
components.purpose: A row of filters the reader switches on and off above the list they narrow, built on native checkboxes or radios.
whenToUse: To narrow a list or a table by a few known values, such as the status of a run or its repository, where the reader should see every choice at once.

Directly above the list it filters, with a line that says how many items match.
whenNotToUse: To switch between two or three views of the same content. Use a segmented control.

To show the filters in force with a way to remove each. Use tags with remove buttons.
