components.name: hover-card
components.title: Hover card
components.purpose: A preview of a linked item, such as a run, a branch or a person, shown beside its link so the reader can decide whether to follow it.
whenToUse: On a link to an item that appears in passing, in a sentence, a row or a transcript, where a few facts save the reader a visit: the status of a run, how far a branch is ahead, who a person is.
Only for facts the linked page also shows. The card is a shortcut to them, never their only home.
whenNotToUse: For anything the reader needs in order to act, or any action. Put it in the view. A hover card may never open, on a touch screen or with a screen reader.
For a line of text about a control. Use a tooltip.
For content opened on purpose from a button, or a small form. Use a popover.
For the details of the selected row beside a list. Use the inspector.
On every link of a dense list. Preview the items that are referred to, not the list's own rows.

variants.name: start
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The card hangs under the link from its leading edge.

variants.name: end
variants.use: A link at the trailing edge of the view. The card lines up with the link's trailing edge and grows towards the start.

variants.name: with a preview button
variants.use: An icon button after the wrapper, with popovertarget pointing at the card, where the preview matters on a touch screen. No modifier class.

accessibility: Wrap the link in a span with the class gw-hover-card, and put the card straight after the link: a span with gw-popover and gw-hover-card__card, an id and popover="hint". Give the link interestfor with the card's id. Use spans inside the card when the link sits in a paragraph, where a div is not allowed.

The card's content is the popover's: gw-popover__title for the item's name, gw-hover-card__meta for one line that places it, and gw-popover__facts for a few labelled values in words, with units. An avatar or a badge may stand in for the title.

The card holds only what the linked page also shows, and no link, button or field. A control inside it could not be found by touch or with a screen reader, so the link is not given aria-describedby or aria-haspopup: following it is the accessible way to the same facts.
With that markup alone the card opens on hover and on keyboard focus with no script, and stays open while the pointer is on it. It closes when the pointer and the focus leave.

A browser with interest invokers also opens it after a long press on a touch screen, closes it on Escape, and draws it in the top layer where no container clips it. Other browsers ignore popover="hint" used this way and interestfor.

A tap follows the link, to the page that holds everything the card shows. Where the preview itself matters on a touch screen, add the preview button: an icon button after the wrapper with popovertarget and a name such as Preview run 4181. A tap on it opens and closes the card.
Shown without the top layer, the card is clipped by an ancestor that hides its overflow. Use gw-hover-card--end at the trailing edge of the view so it stays on the screen.
To fill the card when it opens, the app listens for the card's toggle event, shows a spinner with its text while the facts load, and on failure says to follow the link.

components.name: icon-button
components.title: Icon button
components.purpose: A button that shows only an icon, for a familiar action where a text label has no room.
whenToUse: For a familiar action in a dense row or a toolbar, such as copying a branch name or opening a menu of more actions.
For a toggle that shows or hides part of the view, such as the terminal, with aria-pressed.
whenNotToUse: When the icon would not be understood without words. Use a button with a text label, with or without a leading icon.
For the main action of a view. Use a primary button with a text label.
To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
For a setting that is saved. Use a switch or a checkbox.

variants.name: bordered
variants.use: The default: gw-button gw-icon-button on one element. A standalone action that should read as a control.

variants.name: quiet
variants.use: gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-icon-button. No border until it is hovered or pressed, for a row or a toolbar that holds several.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px square, with a 16px icon. There is no smaller size: do not add gw-button--small, whose target would be narrower than 44px.

accessibility: Use a button element with type="button", carrying gw-button and gw-icon-button. The icon is an svg with class gw-button__icon and aria-hidden="true".

The button must have an accessible name: an aria-label on the button, or text in a span with gw-visually-hidden inside it. The name is a verb and what it acts on, such as Copy branch name, and it names the item when the action repeats in a list, such as More actions for run 2184.

For a toggle, set aria-pressed="true" or "false" and switch it on each press. Keep the same name in both states: the state is announced from aria-pressed. The stylesheet adds a border, a sunken fill and a bar under the icon while it is on.
Disabled, aria-disabled and aria-busy behave as on the button. While busy, the spinner takes the place of the icon and the name says what is happening, such as Copying branch name.
Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.
A tooltip may repeat the name for sighted readers, and is never the only place the name lives.

components.name: inspector
components.title: Inspector
components.purpose: A panel for the details of the item selected in the content beside it, with a title, a close button and sections of labelled values.
whenToUse: When the reader picks an item in a list, a board or a diff and wants its facts while the list stays in view: the branch, timing and usage of a run.
At 768px and up, as the second child of gw-inspector__layout, where it is a column after the content.

Below 768px, either stacked under the content in the same layout, or opened over it as a sheet. The sheet is the app's dialog pattern, a dialog element holding the same aside markup, opened when a row is pressed and closed by the same close button. This component does not style the sheet.
whenNotToUse: For the destinations of the app. Use the sidebar nav.
For an item the reader will work in for a while, such as a transcript. Give it a screen of its own.
For a request that waits for an answer. Use an approval.
For a form with several steps. The panel shows facts and at most a few actions.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 288px wide beside the content at 768px and up, with a rule on its leading edge. Full width under the content below that, with a rule above it.

accessibility: Use an aside with the gw-inspector class and an aria-label that names the item, such as Details of run 4182. Change the label when the selection changes.
gw-inspector__header holds the title, a heading with the gw-inspector__title class at the level the view needs, and the close button.

The close button is a button with the classes gw-button, gw-button--quiet and gw-inspector__close. It holds the x icon with aria-hidden="true" and its name in a gw-visually-hidden span, such as Close details of run 4182. When it is pressed the app removes the aside, or sets the hidden attribute on it, clears the selection and moves focus back to the row that was selected.

Each gw-inspector__section has a heading with the gw-inspector__heading class and a dl with the gw-inspector__facts class. Each fact is a div with the gw-inspector__fact class holding a dt, gw-inspector__label, and a dd, gw-inspector__value. A value is written in words with its unit.
Mark the selected item in the content with aria-current="true", as a list row does, so the reader can tell what the panel describes without relying on position.
Selecting an item does not move focus into the panel. The panel follows the content in the markup, so Tab reaches it after the list.

With nothing selected, either leave the aside out or show one gw-inspector__note sentence that says what to select. While the details are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the aside and show a spinner with text. When the fetch fails, show an alert that says what to do.
The component needs no script of its own. The app fills the panel, sets aria-label and handles the close button.

components.name: kbd
components.title: Kbd
components.purpose: A keyboard key or shortcut named in text, such as Ctrl + K.
whenToUse: To name the shortcut for an action that the view also offers as a control: beside a button, in a sentence of help, or in a list of shortcuts.
To name a key the reader presses in a terminal or a form, such as Enter or Esc.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to learn or reach an action. Every shortcut belongs to a button, a link or a menu item the reader can see and press.
For a command, a path or other text the reader types out. Use a code element.
For something the reader presses on screen. Use a button.
For a status or a count. Use a badge or plain text.

variants.name: key
variants.use: One key: a kbd element with the class gw-kbd.

variants.name: combination
variants.use: Keys pressed together: an outer kbd with gw-kbd__combo holding one gw-kbd per key, with a plus sign and spaces written as text between them.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 12px mono text in a 1px border, about 19px tall. It fits a line of body text, a list row and a small button's row without adding height.

accessibility: Use the kbd element. A screen reader reads the key's text in place, so write the key as a word or a character it can say: Ctrl, Shift, Enter, Esc, Up arrow, K. Do not use a symbol alone for a modifier, because it is read differently by each screen reader or not at all.

A combination is an outer kbd with gw-kbd__combo holding one kbd with gw-kbd per key, joined by a plus sign as text with a space each side: Ctrl + K. A screen reader then reads Ctrl plus K. Never draw the plus with a stylesheet or an icon.
Keys pressed one after the other are separate keys joined by the word then: G then R.
Name the platform's own key. Where the app knows the reader is on a Mac it writes Cmd in place of Ctrl; it does not show both.
A shortcut is never the only way to an action. Show it next to the control that does the same thing, or in a list the reader can open from a visible control.
A key is text. It is not focusable and takes no press, and it has no hover or pressed state.
The app wires the shortcut itself. For a button, set aria-keyshortcuts to the same keys, such as aria-keyshortcuts="Control+K", so assistive technology can report it.

components.name: key-value
components.title: Key-value
components.purpose: Facts about one thing as label and value pairs: stacked on a phone, in two columns at 768px and wider.
whenToUse: For the facts of one run, task, repository or request: its branch, its path, when it started, what it cost.
Inside a card or a disclosure, or straight on the page under a heading.
With mono values for anything the reader may copy or compare character by character: a path, a commit hash, a command, a branch name.
whenNotToUse: For the same facts about several things. Use the data table, where each thing is a row.
For one number that deserves emphasis, with its comparison. Use the stat.
For values the reader edits. Use fields.
For a value the reader copies with one press. Use the copy field.
For a status that needs a tone. Write the status in words as the value, or put one badge in it.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Values in the interface typeface.

variants.name: mono value
variants.use: On a single value, with gw-key-value__value: a path, a hash, a command or a branch name, in the mono typeface. Mix it freely with plain values in one list.

variants.name: empty value

accessibility: Use a dl. Each pair is a div with the class gw-key-value__item, holding one dt, gw-key-value__label, and one dd, gw-key-value__value. A screen reader then announces each value with its label.
The label is a noun in sentence case with no colon. The stylesheet does not add one.
A value is never blank and never a lone dash. When there is none, write it in words: Not set, None opened yet. The quiet colour of the empty variant supports the words and does not replace them.
A number carries its unit, and a time is written so it cannot be misread, inside a time element with a datetime attribute.
A long value wraps inside its column, breaking at any character when it must, so the page never scrolls sideways. Do not truncate a path or a hash.
The component has no controls and needs no script. While the facts load, show a spinner in place of the list; if they cannot be read, an error state.

components.purpose: A text link to another view or another site: in running text, standing alone, external or quiet.
whenToUse: To go to another view, another place in this view or another site.
In running text, as a plain a element with no class.
Standing alone, such as View all runs under a list, with the gw-link class.
With the external-link icon and the hidden hint when the link opens another site in a new tab.
whenNotToUse: For an action that changes something, such as Delete branch or Retry. Use a button.
For the main action of a view, even when it goes to another view. Use a link with the primary button classes.
For the app's main destinations. Use a tab bar, or the sidebar at 768px and wider.
For something unavailable. A link cannot be disabled, so write plain text and say why it is unavailable.

A row that does not navigate uses a div with the class gw-list__content. It is not focusable.

A row has at most one action: a small quiet button inside gw-list__action, after the content. When every row's button has the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the row, such as Remove /srv/workspaces/acme-api.
Mark the row for the view the reader is on with aria-current="page" on its link. It is drawn with a bar and a heavier title as well as a shade.
A leading icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". Trailing text and a status are written in words, never as a colour or an icon alone.
While rows are fetched again, set aria-busy="true" on the list and say so in an element with role="status" outside it.
Tab moves between row links and row actions in order. Enter follows a link. There are no arrow-key bindings.

components.name: listbox
components.title: Listbox
components.purpose: A list of options, always in view, from which the reader selects one or several.
whenToUse: To choose one or several of a known set where the reader benefits from seeing the options and a fact about each, such as branches with how far ahead they are.
As the list of results under a search field, or inside a popover opened from a button that shows the current choice.
With groups when the options fall into a few named sets.
whenNotToUse: In a form that must work with no script. Use a select, radios or checkboxes: a listbox needs the app's keyboard handling.
For two to four short options that fit a row. Use a segmented control or radios.
For a list of actions. Use a menu.
For rows that navigate. Use a list of links.
For filters above a list. Use filter chips.

variants.name: single-select
variants.use: The default. Exactly one option carries aria-selected="true".

variants.name: multi-select
variants.use: Add aria-multiselectable="true" to the listbox. Any number of options carry aria-selected="true". There is no modifier class.

variants.name: grouped
variants.use: Options inside gw-listbox__group elements, each with a gw-listbox__label.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Each option is at least 44px tall and as wide as the listbox.

accessibility: Use a div with the class gw-listbox and role="listbox", named by aria-labelledby pointing at its visible label or by aria-label. Add aria-multiselectable="true" when several options may be selected.

Each option is a div with gw-listbox__option, role="option", an id and aria-selected set to "true" or "false" on every option. The check is drawn by the stylesheet from aria-selected, in a slot every row keeps.
A group is a div with gw-listbox__group, role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-listbox__label, which carries role="presentation".

Trailing text goes in a span with gw-listbox__meta and is part of the option's name. An option that cannot be chosen carries aria-disabled="true", stays in the arrow-key order, and gives its reason in that trailing text.

The keyboard contract is the app's. Focus is roving: exactly one option has tabindex="0", the selected one or else the first, and every other option has tabindex="-1", so Tab enters and leaves the listbox in one stop.

Down and Up move focus to the next and the previous option and stop at the ends. Home and End go to the first and the last. A typed letter moves to the next option that starts with it. On each move the app swaps the tabindex values and calls focus() on the option.
In a single-select listbox, Space or Enter selects the focused option, or selection follows focus where selecting has no side effect. The app sets aria-selected="true" on it and "false" on the rest.

In a multi-select listbox, Space switches the focused option, Shift with Down or Up switches the option moved to, and Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all. A press on an option does the same as Space on it. The app ignores presses on an option with aria-disabled="true".

With no options, loading or after a failed load, keep the gw-listbox box without role="listbox" and put one gw-listbox__note in it: a sentence with role="status" that says what to try, a spinner with its text, or a sentence with role="alert" and a button that loads again. An element with role="listbox" always holds at least one option.

components.name: menu
components.title: Menu
components.purpose: A list of actions on one thing, opened from a button.
whenToUse: For three or more actions on one item that do not all fit beside it, such as the actions on a task or a run.
For the less common actions of a view, behind a button that names what they act on.
whenNotToUse: For one or two actions. Show them as buttons.
For the main action of a view. Show it as the primary button.
To choose a value in a form. Use a select.
To move between views. Use links, a tab bar or a sidebar.
For content that is not a list of actions. Use a popover.

variants.name: item
variants.use: The default item, with no modifier class. An optional gw-menu__icon comes before its text.

variants.name: danger item
variants.use: An item that deletes or cannot be undone. It is last, below a gw-menu__divider, and its label names what is lost.

accessibility: Give the menu the popover attribute, an id, role="menu" and an aria-label. Give the button popovertarget with that id and aria-haspopup="menu". The browser opens and closes the menu, sets aria-expanded on the button, closes on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the button.

Put the menu straight after its button in the markup. Each item is a button with type="button", role="menuitem" and the class gw-menu__item. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
A section is a div with role="group", the class gw-menu__section and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-menu__label, which carries role="presentation". A divider is an hr with gw-menu__divider.

An unavailable item carries aria-disabled="true", so it stays in the arrow-key order and a screen reader can find it, and the app ignores presses on it. Say why in its label when the reason is not obvious.

Without script the menu still works: Tab moves through the items and Enter or Space activates one. The arrow keys are the one thing the app, or the system's behaviours module, adds, as a roving focus: when the menu opens (its toggle event), move focus to the first item. Give every item tabindex="-1" except the one that has focus. Down and Up move focus to the next and the previous item and wrap at the ends, Home and End go to the first and the last, and a letter key goes to the next item that starts with it. Tab closes the menu.
After an item's action runs, the app closes the menu with hidePopover(), and focus returns to the button.

Where the browser supports CSS anchor positioning the menu hangs below its button and flips at the edge of the screen. Elsewhere it sits centred at the bottom of the screen. To open it from script, call showPopover({ source: button }).

components.name: message
components.title: Message
components.purpose: One row of an agent transcript: a prompt, the agent's text, a tool call, its result, a denial, usage or the end of a turn.
whenToUse: For each event of an agent's turn, as a list item in the transcript's ol or ul, oldest first.
To show what a tool was asked to do and what it returned, in mono, at phone width.
whenNotToUse: For a request that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
For the note that the agent is still working. Use streaming as the last row.
For a message about the app itself, such as a lost connection. Use an alert or a banner.

variants.name: agent
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Text the agent wrote. Label it with the agent's name.

variants.name: user
variants.use: A prompt the reader sent. Label it You.

variants.name: tool-call
variants.use: A tool the agent ran: the tool name, then the command or path. Put long arguments in a details element whose summary keeps the label, the tool name and a short command.

variants.name: tool-result
variants.use: What a tool returned. Show the first lines, and put the rest in a details element whose summary reads Show full output.

variants.name: denied
variants.use: A call that was refused. Say what was not run and why.

variants.name: usage
variants.use: A quiet line of figures for the turn, such as tokens and duration.

variants.name: turn-end
variants.use: A quiet closing row under a rule, saying that the turn finished and how: completed, stopped or ended with an error.

accessibility: Each row is an li in an ol or ul. Put role="log" and an accessible name on the list when rows are added while the reader watches, so new rows are announced.

Every row starts with gw-message__label, which says the kind in words: You, Claude Code, Tool call, Tool result, Denied, Usage, End. The kind is never the colour alone, and the denied row's icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Write transcript text as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen.

Collapsed arguments and long output use a native details element, with no script. Its summary holds text that says what is inside. Enter and Space open and close it, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
When output is cut short, the lines after the preview go in the details element, so opened text continues where the preview stopped.
The app sets nothing but the open attribute, which the browser manages.

components.name: notification-list
components.title: Notification list
components.purpose: What happened while the reader was away, grouped as unread and earlier: each entry says what happened, where and when, and offers at most one action.
whenToUse: For the reader's notifications, in a view of their own or in a sheet or popover opened from the app header.
When each entry points at something that changed, such as a run that needs approval, finished or failed, and opening it is the usual next step.
whenNotToUse: For a message about something on the current view. Use an alert, or a toast for a passing confirmation.
For everything that happened during one run. Use the activity feed or the timeline.
For approvals the reader answers in place. Use the approval, or the pending tray for how many wait.
For a list with no read or unread state. Use the list.
accessibility: Wrap everything in a div with gw-notification-list. gw-notification-list__header holds gw-notification-list__heading, with the title as a heading at the level the view needs and a p with gw-notification-list__count that says how many are unread in words, then the Mark all as read button.
Give the count role="status". After Mark all as read, or when a notification arrives, the app changes its text, such as All read or 3 unread, and a screen reader announces it.
Mark all as read is a gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small. Disable it when nothing is unread. It marks the notifications read and moves them under Earlier; it deletes nothing.
Each group is a heading with gw-notification-list__group, Unread or Earlier, one level below the title, followed by a ul with the class gw-list. Leave a group out when it has no entries.

Each entry is an li with gw-list__row and gw-notification-list__item holding one a with gw-list__link that opens the thing the notification is about. Inside it, gw-list__primary says what happened in a sentence that names the thing, gw-list__secondary says where, and gw-list__meta holds when, in a time element with a datetime attribute.

An unread entry starts its gw-list__secondary with a span with gw-notification-list__unread holding the word Unread. The stylesheet draws the dot before it, so unread is never a dot or a colour alone. Following the link marks the entry read: the app removes that span.

An entry has at most one action, and only when the reader can settle it from here: a gw-button gw-button--small inside a div with gw-list__action and gw-notification-list__action, after the link, never primary. Its aria-label starts with its visible words and names the thing, such as Review request for run 2292. Below 768px it sits under the entry's text.
Tab moves through each entry's link and then its action. Enter follows the link. There are no arrow-key bindings, and the component needs no script.
While the notifications load, show a spinner in place of the groups. If they cannot be read, an error state with Retry. When there are none at all, an empty state that says what will appear here.

components.name: number-field
components.title: Number field
components.purpose: A numeric input as the control of a field, with an optional unit written beside it and optional stepper buttons.
whenToUse: For an amount the reader types or nudges: a timeout in minutes, a retry count, a spending limit.
With stepper buttons when the value is small and usually changes by a step or two.
With a unit whenever the number alone could be misread.
whenNotToUse: For a number that is a name, such as a run number, a port or a one-time code. Use a field with inputmode="numeric", or the one-time-code input.
For a rough amount where the exact figure does not matter. Use a slider.
For one of a few fixed amounts. Use a select or a radio group.
For a date or a time. Use a date field.

variants.name: plain
variants.use: The input alone inside gw-number-field.

variants.name: with a unit
variants.use: A span with gw-number-field__unit after the input, holding the unit as a word.

variants.name: with steppers
variants.use: Two icon buttons with gw-number-field__step at the end of the row: decrease first, then increase.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and at most 264px wide. Each stepper is 44px square.

accessibility: Use input type="number" carrying gw-field__control and gw-number-field__input, inside a div with gw-number-field, inside gw-field. The label, description and error are the field's.
Set min, max and step on the input, and say the range in the description. Set inputmode="numeric" for whole numbers and inputmode="decimal" when step is a fraction, so a phone shows the right keys.
Write the unit as a word in a span with gw-number-field__unit, give it an id and list that id first in the input's aria-describedby, so a screen reader hears Run timeout, 30, minutes.

A stepper is a button with type="button" and the classes gw-button, gw-icon-button and gw-number-field__step, holding the minus or plus icon with aria-hidden="true" and a gw-visually-hidden name that says what it changes and by how much, such as Increase the run timeout by 5 minutes.
The app wires the steppers: on a press it calls stepDown() or stepUp() on the input and dispatches an input event. It sets disabled on the decrease button at min and on the increase button at max.
The Up and Down arrow keys step the value while the input has focus. That comes from the input, and the browser's own small spin buttons are hidden.
For a value out of range, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that repeats the value and gives the limit.
When the input is disabled, set disabled on both steppers too.

components.name: otp-input
components.title: One-time-code input
components.purpose: A single input for a short one-time code, drawn with wide letter spacing so each digit can be checked.
whenToUse: For the code from an authenticator app, a text message or an email, when signing in or confirming a risky change.
For any short code the reader copies from somewhere else, digit by digit or by pasting.
whenNotToUse: For a password or a passphrase. Use a password field.
For a long recovery code or an access token. Use a field with the mono type of a textarea, or a plain field.
For an amount. Use a number field.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and at most 242px wide, with 20px mono digits. It fits eight digits.

accessibility: Use one input with type="text" carrying gw-field__control and gw-otp-input, inside gw-field. The label says where the code comes from, and the description says how many digits it has and where it was sent.

Set autocomplete="one-time-code", so a phone offers the code from the message it just received, and inputmode="numeric" for the number keys. Use type="text", never type="number": a code may start with a zero and is not an amount.
Do not set maxlength. A code pasted as 482 913 would lose its last digit. The app strips spaces and hyphens from the value, then checks the length.
Never split the code across several inputs, and never move focus or send the form by script as the last digit arrives. The reader sends it with the form's button or with Enter.

For a wrong or expired code, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that says which it was and what to do, with the action it names, such as Send a new code, as a button beside the field. Leave the code in the input so it can be corrected.
While the code is checked, set disabled on the input and say so in the description with role="status".
The keyboard is the text input's own, and pasting works as in any field.

components.purpose: The top of a view: its title, an optional one-line description and the view's one optional primary action.
whenToUse: Once, at the top of a view's content, to say what the view is.
With the action when the view has one main thing to do, such as New task on the task list.
In the compact variant above a board, a transcript or a diff, where the content needs the height.
whenNotToUse: For the bar across the top of the app with the product name and the back link. Use an app header.
For the heading of a section inside a view. Use a plain h2.

components.name: pagination
components.title: Pagination
components.purpose: Previous and next for a list split into pages, with the position written in words and optional numbered pages.
whenToUse: Under a list or table that is split into pages the reader may want to return to by number or by address, such as finished runs.
With numbered pages when the reader jumps around, such as to the last page. They show at 768px and up only.
whenNotToUse: For a list of one page. Show no pagination at all.
To reveal the rest of a short list in place. Use show more, with its Show all button.
For a transcript or a log that grows while the reader watches. Load older lines as the reader scrolls back.
For the steps of a form. Use buttons named for each step.

variants.name: previous and next
variants.use: The default: the status and the two buttons. The whole component at phone width.

variants.name: numbered

components.name: password-field
components.title: Password field
components.purpose: A password input as the control of a field, with a button that shows or hides what was typed.
whenToUse: For a password, a passphrase or another secret the reader types or pastes and may want to check: a registry password, a deploy key passphrase.
For signing in and for choosing a new password, with the autocomplete value that fits each.
whenNotToUse: For a one-time code from a message or an authenticator app. Use the one-time-code input.
For a secret the app made and the reader only copies, such as an access token. Use a copy field.
For text that is not secret. Use a field.

variants.name: with a show button
variants.use: The default. A button with gw-password-field__toggle after the input.

variants.name: input alone
variants.use: The same input with no button, only where the password is pasted by a script and never typed.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as the field. The button is 60px wide and 44px tall.

accessibility: Use input type="password" carrying gw-field__control and gw-password-field__input, inside a div with gw-password-field, inside gw-field. The label, description and error are the field's.

Set autocomplete="current-password" where the reader enters a password they already have and autocomplete="new-password" where they choose one, with a stable name attribute. Never set autocomplete="off", and never block pasting. Add autocapitalize="none" and spellcheck="false".

The button is a button with type="button", the class gw-password-field__toggle and aria-controls pointing at the input. It takes no aria-pressed: its words change with its state, and a pressed state on top of them would say it twice. It holds two spans, gw-password-field__show and gw-password-field__hide, each a word followed by a gw-visually-hidden span that names the password: Show the registry password, Hide the registry password.

The stylesheet draws one of the two spans, chosen from the input's type, and hides the other from screen readers too. So the button's name changes in words with its state, and the app never rewrites the label.

The app does one thing on a press: it sets the input's type to text, and on the next press back to password. It sets the type back to password before the form is sent, so the browser does not remember the value as plain text.

Caps Lock and strength messages are the app's. Write them as text in a second gw-field__description with aria-live="polite", listed in the input's aria-describedby. A strength message is words, such as Too short: 9 of 16 characters, never a colour bar alone.

State the rule for a new password in the description before the reader types. For a rejected password, set aria-invalid="true" and link a gw-field__error that says what to do next. Do not clear the input.
Tab reaches the input and then the button. Enter and Space press the button, and focus stays on it.
When the input is disabled, set disabled on the button too.

components.name: popover
components.title: Popover
components.purpose: A small panel beside the button that opens it, for short supplementary content or a small form, which does not block the page.
whenToUse: For a few facts or a short explanation most readers can do without.
For a small form of one or two fields that belongs to the control beside it, such as renaming one item.
whenNotToUse: For a list of actions. Use a menu.
For a line of supplementary text about a control. Use a tooltip.
For anything the reader must see or answer, such as an error or an approval. Show it in the view.
For a task that must be finished or cancelled. Use a dialog.
For a longer form. Use a sheet.
accessibility: Give the panel the popover attribute and an id, and give the button popovertarget with that id. The browser then opens and closes the panel, sets aria-expanded on the button, closes on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the button. No script is needed.
Put the panel straight after its button in the markup, so Tab goes from the button into the panel.
The button's label says what the popover holds, such as Show run cost. When the panel has a title, point aria-labelledby at it.
A popover is a view of its own: it may hold one primary button. A Cancel button inside it carries popovertarget with the panel's id and popovertargetaction="hide".

Where the browser supports CSS anchor positioning, the panel hangs below its button and flips above it or to its other edge at the edge of the screen. Elsewhere it sits centred at the bottom of the screen.
To move focus into a small form when it opens, put autofocus on its first field. To open the popover from script, call showPopover({ source: button }) so the panel still knows its button.
While the content loads, show a spinner with its text. If loading fails, say what happened and what to do, in the panel.

components.name: progress
components.title: Progress
components.purpose: How far a job with a known length has got: a labelled bar on a native progress element, with the value written in words.
whenToUse: For work that can be counted: 7 of 12 checks passed, 96 of 213 tests run, 31 of 48 files uploaded.
In the indeterminate form, for the first moments of such a job, before its length is known. Switch to the determinate form as soon as there is a total.
whenNotToUse: For a wait with no length at all. Use a spinner, with text that says what is happening.
In place of content that is loading. Use a skeleton.
For a status, such as Finished or Failed. Use a badge, or plain text.
For a measurement that is not progress, such as disk space used. Write it as text: 412 MB of 20 GB is free.

variants.name: determinate
variants.use: The progress element has value and max. The fill is as wide as value over max.

variants.name: indeterminate
variants.use: The progress element has no value attribute. The whole bar is one mid tone that fades slowly, and holds still under reduced motion. The value text says what is happening.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The bar is 8px tall and as wide as its container, under a row that holds the label and the value.

accessibility: Markup, in this order: a label with the gw-progress__label class and a for attribute, a p with the gw-progress__value class, and a progress element with the gw-progress__bar class and the id the label names. The stylesheet draws the bar under the two lines of text.
The label says what is measured. The value is a sentence with the count, the total and the unit: 7 of 12 checks passed. Never a bare number or a bare percentage.
Set value and max on the progress element to the same two numbers, and aria-valuetext to the same sentence, so a screen reader says the count in words instead of a percentage.
As work goes on, the app updates three things together: the value attribute, aria-valuetext, and the text of gw-progress__value. It sets no inline style and no class.
For the indeterminate form, leave the value attribute off, and remove it with removeAttribute to go back to that form. The value text says what is happening, such as Counting objects.
Do not make the value text a live region: a count that changes every second would be read out every second. When the job ends, announce the result once, in an alert or a status message.
The bar has no controls and takes no focus. The component needs no script beyond those updates.

components.name: radio
components.title: Radio
components.purpose: A native radio group: exactly one of a few options, each with room for a full label and a description, sent with a form.
whenToUse: To choose exactly one of two to six options that need a full label or a line of description each.
When the reader should see every option before choosing.
whenNotToUse: For two to five options with one- or two-word labels. Use a segmented control.
For more than six options. Use a select.
For options where any number may be chosen. Use checkboxes.
For a single on-or-off setting. Use a switch, or a checkbox inside a form.
accessibility: Use a fieldset with gw-radio__group and a legend with gw-radio__legend that asks the question. Each option is a div with gw-radio holding input type="radio" with gw-radio__input, then a label with gw-radio__label whose for attribute is the input's id.
Every input in a group has the same name attribute, and a different name from every other group on the page.
The options are one above the other. The input comes first in each row: the stylesheet reads its state to style the label after it.
A description is a p with gw-radio__description, linked from its input with aria-describedby.

Tab moves into the group, to the chosen option or the first one. The arrow keys move between options and choose as they go, and Space chooses the focused option. All of it comes from the native inputs.
The circle is drawn 20px across and its pointer target is 44px; a press on the label chooses the option too.

whenToUse: For the reasoning an agent wrote before its answer, above that answer in a transcript row.

whenNotToUse: For the answer itself, or anything the reader must read. Use a message.
For tool arguments or output. Use a message's details, or a tool call.
For anything that holds an action. An action goes beside the answer, or in an approval when the agent is waiting on it.
For settings or secondary content of a view. Use a disclosure.

The text is muted on the page surface. Do not place the component on a sunken or tinted surface, where muted text is too faint.
Enter and Space open and close the summary, and its pointer target is 44px tall. The component needs no script.

components.name: run-status
components.title: Run status
components.purpose: The content of one list row that summarises a run or a task: its title, its station as a badge in words, who or what is acting and the elapsed time.
whenToUse: For each row of a list of runs or tasks, where the reader scans for the ones that need them.
When a row needs the station, the actor and the elapsed time together, and at most one action.
whenNotToUse: For a row with only a title and one trailing fact. Use the list's own parts.
For the heading of a run's own view. Use a page header with a badge beside the title.
For what happened during a run, entry by entry. Use an activity feed.
For runs compared across several columns. Use a table.

variants.name: link
variants.use: Inside an a element with the class gw-list__link, so the whole row opens the run.

variants.name: static
variants.use: Inside a div with the class gw-list__content, for a row that does not navigate.

accessibility: It is the content of a list row: a span with the class gw-run-status inside the gw-list__link or gw-list__content of an li with the class gw-list__row, in a ul with the class gw-list. Every part is a span, so it is valid inside a link.

The parts come in reading order: gw-run-status__title, gw-run-status__station, gw-run-status__facts. A screen reader reads the row as its title, its station, then who is acting and for how long. Below 768px the station sits under the title, and from 768px the row is one line with the station at its end.

gw-run-status__station holds one badge with the station in words: Queued, Building, Verifying, Reviewing, Awaiting decision, Blocked, Interrupted or Decided. Use the same word, tone and icon for a station everywhere. The badge icon carries aria-hidden="true".

gw-run-status__facts says who or what is acting in words, such as Claude Code, implementer or Waiting on you, then the elapsed time in a time element with the class gw-run-status__elapsed and a datetime duration. Write the time with its unit: 4 min 12 s. A time that ticks is not in a live region.

A row has at most one action, and only when the run waits on the reader: a gw-button gw-button--small in the row's gw-list__action, after the link, never primary. Its aria-label starts with its visible words and names the run, such as Resume Fix the login timeout.
When a station changes while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the row.
Tab reaches the row's link and then its action. Enter follows the link. The component needs no script.

components.name: search-field
components.title: Search field
components.purpose: A search input with a search icon, an optional clear button and a line that counts the results.
whenToUse: To search or filter a list the reader can see, such as runs, branches or changed files.
At the top of the list it filters, with the count line between the field and the results.
whenNotToUse: For any other text value, such as a branch name to create. Use a field.
To pick one of a known, short set. Use a select or a segmented control.
As the only way to reach an item. The list stays browsable without a search.

variants.name: visible label
variants.use: The default. A label with gw-search-field__label above the input.

variants.name: hidden label
variants.use: The same label with gw-visually-hidden added, where the list's heading already says what is searched. The label element stays in the markup.

variants.name: with a clear button
variants.use: A button with gw-search-field__clear after the input. Leave it out where the field is cleared some other way.

accessibility: Use input type="search" carrying gw-field__control and gw-search-field__input, inside a div with gw-search-field__box. The search icon is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup.
Every search field has a label element with gw-search-field__label tied to the input by for and id. Add gw-visually-hidden to hide it from sight. A placeholder is a hint, never the label.

The outer element with gw-search-field is a form with role="search" and an aria-label when it is the search for the page, and a plain div when it filters one list in place. Give each search landmark on a page a different label.

The clear button is a button with gw-search-field__clear, placed after the input, holding its name in a span with gw-visually-hidden, such as Clear the search. Its cross is drawn by the stylesheet and its target is 44px square.

With type="reset" inside a form the clear button needs no script, as long as the form is served with an empty value. Otherwise use type="button", and the app empties the input and moves focus back to it.
The clear button is hidden while the input is empty. That relies on the input having a placeholder attribute: give it hint text, or a single space where no hint is wanted.

The count line is a p with gw-search-field__count and aria-live="polite". Keep it in the page from the start, and change only its text when the results change, after the reader pauses typing, so a screen reader announces the new count without losing focus. It gives a number and its unit, such as 3 of 128 runs match "session".
While results load, the count line says what is being searched. With no results it says so, repeats the query and says what to try next. The stylesheet has no styling of its own for either.
When the input is disabled, say why in the count line and link it with aria-describedby. Leave aria-live off a line that never changes.
Tab reaches the input and then the clear button. Escape clears the input in browsers that support it for a search input, and Enter submits the form.

components.name: segmented-control
components.title: Segmented control
components.purpose: Two to five short options of which exactly one is chosen, shown side by side.
whenToUse: To switch how the same content is shown, such as a unified or a split diff.
To filter a list by one of a few values, such as the status of a run.
When every option has a label of one or two words and all of them should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For more than five options, or labels longer than two words. Use a select or a radio group.
To move between views or pages. Use links, or the tab bar for an app's main destinations.
For a single on-or-off setting. Use a switch.
For actions, such as Rerun failed and Rerun all. Use an attached button group.
accessibility: Use a fieldset with gw-segmented-control and a legend with gw-segmented-control__legend that names the choice. Add gw-visually-hidden to the legend where a heading beside the control already names it. The legend stays in the markup.

Inside a div with gw-segmented-control__options, each option is a label with gw-segmented-control__option holding input type="radio" with gw-segmented-control__input and then a span with gw-segmented-control__label. The label element names the radio, and the span must come straight after the input.
Every input has the same name attribute, different from every other group on the page, and one input has the checked attribute from the start.
It needs no script: the browser keeps exactly one option chosen. An app that reacts at once listens for the change event on the fieldset.
The chosen option is a raised segment with a border and heavier text, so it does not rest on colour.
Disable one option with the disabled attribute on its input, or the whole control with disabled on the fieldset.
Tab moves into the control, to the chosen option. The arrow keys move between options and choose as they go. All of it comes from the native radios.

Each segment is at least 44px wide and its pointer target is 44px tall. The segments share the row equally at every width, and a label too long for its segment wraps inside it, so the control never scrolls sideways.

components.name: select
components.title: Select
components.purpose: A native select as the control of a field, for one choice from a short fixed list.
whenToUse: For one choice from a list the app already knows: a base branch, a repository, a model.
When the list is too long to show as radio buttons, from about five options up.
whenNotToUse: For two to four options the reader should compare. Use a radio group.
For on or off. Use a checkbox.
For a list long enough to need searching, or for free text. Use a text input in a field.
For a menu of actions. Use buttons.

sizes.name: default

accessibility: Use a select element carrying both gw-field__control and gw-select__control, wrapped in an element with gw-select, inside gw-field. The wrapper only draws the chevron.
Give it a label element whose for attribute matches the select's id.
When nothing is chosen yet, make the first option an instruction with an empty value, such as Choose a repository, and set required on the select.
For an invalid choice, set aria-invalid="true" on the select and link a gw-field__error that says what to choose.

The keyboard is the browser's own: Space or Enter opens the list, the arrow keys move, typing jumps to a matching option, Escape closes.

components.name: selection-basket
components.title: Selection basket
components.purpose: The bar that appears while rows of a list or a table are selected: how many are selected, one bulk action, a More menu and Clear selection.
whenToUse: When the reader ticks rows in a list or a table and then acts on all of them at once: archive, re-run, delete.
Once per list, placed straight after the list it acts on, in the same container.
whenNotToUse: For the actions on one row. Put one quiet action in the row, or a menu.
For actions that do not depend on a selection, such as New task. Put them in the page header.
For filters on the list. Use the search field or a sheet of filters.
To report what a bulk action did. Use a toast, or the undo toast when it can be taken back.

variants.name: secondary action
variants.use: The default. The bulk action is a gw-button gw-button--small, for a view that already has a primary action.

variants.name: primary action
variants.use: The bulk action is a gw-button gw-button--primary gw-button--small. Only when the view has no other primary action while rows are selected.

accessibility: Use a div with gw-selection-basket, role="region" and an aria-label that says what is selected, such as Selected runs. The region is then a landmark a screen reader can jump to from anywhere in the list.

gw-selection-basket__selection holds the count and then Clear selection. The count is a p with gw-selection-basket__count and role="status" that says the number and the thing in words: 3 runs selected. The app rewrites it whenever the selection changes, and a screen reader announces the new count.

Keep the basket in the page from the start with the hidden attribute. On the first selection remove hidden and then set the count's text, so the count is announced. When the selection is cleared, set hidden again and move focus back to the list if it was inside the basket.
Clear selection is a gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small. It unticks every row and changes nothing else.

gw-selection-basket__actions holds at most one bulk action as a button whose words name the action and the count, such as Archive 3 runs, and then, when there are more actions, one More button that opens a menu from the menu component. A bulk action that deletes sits last in the menu as a danger item and opens a confirm dialog.
The buttons are drawn 32px tall and their pointer targets are 44px. The bulk action is never one of two primary buttons in the view.

While the bulk action runs, set aria-busy="true" on its button, change its words to say what is happening, and disable the other buttons. If it fails, add a p with gw-selection-basket__error and role="alert" as the last child, saying how many were not done and what to do, and keep the selection.

The basket sticks to the bottom of the screen while the list it follows is in view, above the home indicator on a phone, so give the list's container enough bottom padding that the last row can scroll clear of it.
Tab reaches Clear selection, the bulk action and More, in that order, after the last row of the list. The menu's keys are those of the menu component.

components.name: settings-row
components.title: Settings row
components.purpose: One setting as a row: its label and a one-line description, with a single control or a status at the far end.
whenToUse: For a page of settings that each take effect by themselves: a switch, a choice from a short list, an account to connect.
For a group of related settings under one heading, such as Notifications or Connected accounts.
For a destructive setting, such as deleting a workspace, in a group of its own at the end of the page.
whenNotToUse: For values sent together with one button. Use fields in a form.
For a setting that needs more than one control or more than a line of explanation. Give it a view or a sheet of its own, and make the row's control a button that opens it.
For facts the reader cannot change. Use the key-value list.
For a list of things the reader opens. Use the list.

variants.name: switch
variants.use: The row holds one gw-switch and nothing else. The switch brings its own label, description, state in words and error.

variants.name: select
variants.use: gw-settings-row__text, then gw-settings-row__control holding a gw-select. The label is a label element for the select.

variants.name: button
variants.use: gw-settings-row__control holds one gw-button whose words name the action and the thing, such as Connect GitHub. Never primary.

variants.name: status
variants.use: gw-settings-row__control holds a p with gw-settings-row__status that says the state in words, such as Signed in as mira@acme.dev.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: A setting that deletes or cannot be undone. The label gets a warning mark, the description names what is lost and the control is a gw-button gw-button--danger that opens a confirm dialog.

accessibility: A group is a div with gw-settings-row__group, role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-settings-row__heading, a heading at the level the page needs. Each row is a div with gw-settings-row.
A row has one control. For a switch, put the gw-switch markup in the row by itself: its label and description stand in for gw-settings-row__text.

For a select, gw-settings-row__label is a label element whose for attribute is the select's id, and the select points at gw-settings-row__description with aria-describedby. The select saves on its change event, so the row needs no Save button.

For a button or a status, gw-settings-row__label is a p. The button's own words say what it does and to what, so it reads correctly out of context, and it points at the description with aria-describedby.
The description is one line that says what the setting does or what state it is in. A status, such as Connected or Not connected, is written in words.
When a control is unavailable, set the disabled attribute and say why in the description.
While a button's action runs, set aria-busy="true" on it and change its words to say what is happening, such as Connecting to GitHub.

If a change is not saved, put the control back to the saved value and add a p with gw-settings-row__error and role="alert" as the row's last child. It says what the setting still is and what to do, and its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
A danger row's label is marked with an icon as well as the danger button's colour. Its button never deletes at once: it opens a confirm dialog that names the thing.
Below 768px the control sits under the text; from 768px it is at the far end of the row, centred on the text. Tab moves through the controls in order. The component needs no script.

components.name: sheet
components.title: Sheet
components.purpose: A panel for a longer form or the details of an item, rising from the bottom edge on a phone and sitting as a side panel at 768px and wider.
whenToUse: For a form too long for a dialog, such as a new task or a set of filters.
To show the details of one item without leaving the list it came from.
whenNotToUse: For one question or one field. Use a dialog.
To confirm deleting something. Use the confirm dialog.
For a few lines of supplementary content beside a control. Use a popover.
For a list of actions. Use a menu.
For content the reader should be able to link to or come back to. Give it a view of its own.
accessibility: Use a dialog element with the class gw-sheet and aria-labelledby pointing at gw-sheet__title, an h2.

Open it with the one line document.getElementById("sheet-id").showModal(). That call traps focus, makes the page behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener. As progressive enhancement the opener may carry command="show-modal" and commandfor="sheet-id". Do not write the open attribute yourself: the examples carry it only so they are drawn in the gallery.

gw-sheet__header is a form with method="dialog" holding the title and the Close button, so Close works with no script. Close is a quiet button with only an icon, and its aria-label says what it closes.
The body is gw-sheet__body and scrolls. The footer is gw-sheet__footer, outside the body, and holds the sheet's one primary button first. Never put the primary action in the body.

When the footer's button submits fields in the body, wrap the body and the footer in a second form with the class gw-sheet__form. With method="dialog" its buttons close the sheet and the app reads dialog.returnValue in a close event listener. To validate or save first, handle the submit event and call preventDefault().
A body with no control in it that may scroll takes tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label, so the keyboard can scroll it.

The sheet slides in when showModal() opens it and the reset removes the movement for readers who ask for reduced motion. It keeps clear of the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), which needs viewport-fit=cover in the page's viewport meta tag to be more than zero.

While the body loads, show a spinner with its text in the body. If loading fails, show an alert there that says what to do. While the form is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button and disable the other footer buttons.

components.name: show-more
components.title: Show more
components.purpose: A control after the first part of long content that reveals the rest: a details element for text, code or a log, and a quiet button for a list cut short.
whenToUse: For a log, an output or a description that is long, when its first lines are enough for most readers and the rest is already in the page.
With the Show all button, under a list that shows its first rows, when the full list is short enough to read in one view, about fifty rows at most.
whenNotToUse: For detail under a title of its own, such as Environment. Use a disclosure, whose summary names what it holds.
For a list of hundreds of rows. Use pagination.
For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical in the hidden part fails the hidden-critical-action rule.
For content that fits in a few lines. Show all of it.

variants.name: details
variants.use: gw-show-more__rest is a details element after the part that is always shown. Its summary, gw-show-more__toggle, holds two spans: gw-show-more__more, such as Show 38 more lines, and gw-show-more__less, Show less. The stylesheet shows the one that applies. Needs no script.

variants.name: list
variants.use: A button with the classes gw-button, gw-button--quiet and gw-show-more__all after a gw-list, reading Show all 24 tasks. The app adds the rows when it is pressed.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The control is 44px tall, as wide as its text, and starts at the content's leading edge.

accessibility: Wrap the part that is always shown and the control in a div with the gw-show-more class. The shown part comes first.

Details variant: the app writes the count into gw-show-more__more when it renders, as the number of hidden units and the unit in words: Show 38 more lines, Show 2 more paragraphs. The count is the total minus what is shown. gw-show-more__less always reads Show less.

Only one of the two spans is rendered at a time, so the summary's name is Show 38 more lines while closed and Show less while open, and the browser announces collapsed or expanded with it. The summary always holds text.
Once open, the control is drawn under the revealed content, and stays before it in the markup. Focus stays on the control, and the next Tab or reading step goes into the revealed content.

List variant: the button's label gives the full count and the noun, Show all 24 tasks. When it is pressed the app appends the remaining rows to the same list, removes the button, and moves focus to the first new row. There is no Show less.

While the rows are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the button and change its label to Loading 21 more tasks. If the fetch fails, restore the label and add a p with the gw-show-more__error class and role="alert" before the button, saying what to do.
Tab reaches the control. Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the summary or the button element.
The browser's find-in-page opens a closed details that holds a match.

components.name: sidebar-nav
components.title: Sidebar nav
components.purpose: The destinations of an app in a column beside the content at 768px and up, each with an icon and a text label, grouped into labelled sections.
whenToUse: For moving between the screens of an app at 768px and wider, as the first child of gw-sidebar-layout.

Together with the tab bar: the sidebar is not shown below 768px, where the tab bar lists the two to five main destinations along the bottom. Put both in the markup, with the same destinations in the same order.
When there are more destinations than a tab bar holds. The sidebar lists them all, in sections, and the tab bar keeps the five most used.
whenNotToUse: Below 768px. It is not shown there, so use the tab bar for the main destinations.
For switching between panels inside one view. Use tabs.
For the details of a selected item beside the content. Use the inspector.
For an action such as New task. A destination is a screen, so use a button in the view.
For a screen that does not exist yet. List only screens that exist.

variants.name: with sections
variants.use: Each gw-sidebar-nav__section holds a gw-sidebar-nav__heading and a gw-sidebar-nav__items list. Use it for six destinations or more.

variants.name: flat
variants.use: One gw-sidebar-nav__items list directly in the nav, with no section and no heading. Use it for five destinations or fewer.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 220px wide, with each item 44px tall. Shown only at 768px and up.

accessibility: Use a nav element with an aria-label, such as Main. When the tab bar is also in the markup it may carry the same label, because only one of the two is ever shown and the other is out of the accessibility tree.

Each list of items is a ul of li, each holding one link with the gw-sidebar-nav__item class. A section's heading is a p with an id, and the section's ul points at it with aria-labelledby, so the list is announced by its section name.

Set aria-current="page" on the link for the screen that is open, and on no other. It draws the bar, the shade and the heavier label, and is what a screen reader announces. Never mark the current item with a class.

Every item has a text label in gw-sidebar-nav__label. The icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". A label too long for the column is cut with an ellipsis, so keep labels to one to three words.
Tab moves through the items in order and Enter follows one. Both come from the link element.
Keep the items in the same order on every screen.
gw-sidebar-nav__footer is optional and comes last. It holds a gw-sidebar-nav__items list or a gw-sidebar-nav__note, such as the repository and runner in use.
The component needs no script. The app sets aria-current on the right link when the screen changes.

components.name: skeleton
components.title: Skeleton
components.purpose: Plain shapes that stand where content is about to appear, so the page keeps its layout while it loads.
whenToUse: While a list, a description or a block of content is fetched, when its shape is known and it usually arrives within a few seconds.
On the first load of a view. The shapes match what will replace them: as many rows as usually show, lines the length of the text.
whenNotToUse: When the shape of what is coming is not known, or the wait is an action the reader started. Use a spinner, with text that says what is happening.
When the wait has a measurable length, such as 7 of 12 checks. Use progress.
Together with a spinner for the same wait. Use one of the two.
After the fetch has failed, or after about ten seconds. Replace it with an error state that says what to do: a skeleton that never resolves is a broken promise.
While content already on screen is refreshed. Keep the content and set aria-busy on its container.
For text that is streaming in. Use streaming.

variants.name: line
variants.use: A bar 12px tall in the space of one line of text, as wide as its container. For a paragraph or a set of facts, one above the other.

variants.name: medium line
variants.use: With gw-skeleton__line: 60% of the width, for a title or the last line of a paragraph.

variants.name: short line
variants.use: With gw-skeleton__line: 35% of the width, for a label, a branch name or a time.

variants.name: row
variants.use: A list row at least 44px tall, holding one or two lines. Its container also takes gw-skeleton--rows, so the rows touch and are divided by a rule, as list rows are.

variants.name: block
variants.use: A rectangle 132px tall and as wide as its container, for a code block or a diff.

accessibility: The container is a div with the gw-skeleton class and aria-busy="true". Its first child is a span with the gw-visually-hidden class that says what is loading, such as Loading tasks. The shapes are empty span elements and are not read out.

When the content arrives, the app replaces the whole container with it. Nothing of the skeleton stays, so aria-busy goes with it. When the skeleton stands inside a region that stays, such as a section with a heading, put aria-busy on that region and remove it when the content arrives.
When the fetch fails, or has taken about ten seconds, the app replaces the container with an error state that says what happened and offers Retry.
The shapes fade slowly between full and partial strength. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is off and the shapes hold still.
A skeleton has no controls and takes no focus. If the content it replaces had focus, move focus to the view's heading until the content is back.
The component needs no script beyond the app swapping it for the content.

whenToUse: For an amount where the feel matters more than the figure, across a short range: how many agents work at once, how much effort to spend.
For a scale of a few named steps, such as Low to Maximum, where order matters.
When the effect is shown or applied as the thumb moves.
whenNotToUse: For an exact amount, or a range with more than about twenty steps. Use a number field.
For two to four options that are not a scale. Use a radio group or a segmented control.
For on or off. Use a switch.
To show how far something has got. Use progress or a usage meter.

variants.use: The value is a number with its unit, such as 4 agents.

variants.name: named steps
variants.use: Each step has a name, written in the output and repeated in aria-valuetext on the input.

accessibility: Use a div with gw-slider holding, in this order: a label with gw-slider__label, an output with gw-slider__value, a div with gw-slider__track around an input type="range" with gw-slider__input, then a span with gw-slider__min and a span with gw-slider__max.
The label's for attribute matches the input's id. Set min, max, step and value on the input.

The output holds the current value in words with its unit, and its for attribute names the input. The app rewrites its text on the input's input event. An output is a live region, so a screen reader announces the new words after the thumb moves.
When a step has a name, or the bare number would mislead, also set aria-valuetext on the input to the same words, so the slider itself is read as High and not as 3.
The two spans say what the lowest and highest values are, in words. They are plain text, and the range itself comes from min and max.
The keyboard is the browser's own: Left and Down lower the value by one step, Right and Up raise it, Page Up and Page Down move further, Home and End go to the ends.
The track wrapper reaches 10px past the slider on each side, which is the unpainted part of the thumb's pointer target. Keep at least that much padding between a slider and the edge of the screen.

For several sources in a row that wraps.

For a status. Use a badge.
For a file attached to a prompt, which can be removed. Use an attachment chip.
For a value the reader copies, such as a branch name. Use a copy field.

components.name: sparkline
components.title: Sparkline
components.purpose: A small trend line beside a value, with words that say the trend and the latest value.
whenToUse: Beside a number in a table cell or a stat, to show how it moved over the last few runs or days.
For one series of 5 to 30 points where the shape matters and the single values do not.
whenNotToUse: By itself, with no value and no words. The line cannot be read as a number.
When the reader needs single values, axes or more than one series. Use a table, or a chart the app builds for the purpose.
For progress towards a known total. Use the progress bar or the usage meter.
For one number with its comparison and nothing over time. Use the stat alone.
As decoration on a card or a heading.

variants.name: with words
variants.use: The default. gw-sparkline__text after the drawing says the trend, the period and the latest value in a short visible line.

variants.name: words for screen readers only
variants.use: The same sentence in a span with gw-visually-hidden in place of gw-sparkline__text, where the value and the period are already visible in the same row and a table has no room for the line of text.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 64px wide and 16px tall, with a 1.5px line. It fits a table row and a line of text without adding height.

accessibility: Use a span with the class gw-sparkline holding the svg and then the words. The svg carries aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false": the drawing is not announced, and the words carry everything it shows.

The words are required. They say the direction, the period and the latest value with its unit, such as Rising over the last 7 runs, now 6 min 12 s. Put them in gw-sparkline__text, or in gw-visually-hidden when the same row already shows the value. Direction is a word, Rising, Falling or Steady, never the line's slope or a colour alone.

The app generates the svg: viewBox="0 0 64 16", one polyline with the class gw-sparkline__line, and one circle with the class gw-sparkline__last and r="2" on the last point. Spread the points evenly from x=2 to x=62 and scale the values so the lowest is at y=14 and the highest at y=2. When every value is the same, draw the line at y=8.

The line and the dot are drawn in the main text colour through currentColor, in both themes. Do not set a stroke or fill attribute, and do not add a fill under the line, a gradient, grid lines or an animation.
Do not colour the line by whether the change is good or bad. If that judgement matters, write it in the words.
With fewer than two values there is no line. Leave the svg out and write that in gw-sparkline__text: Not enough runs for a trend yet.
The component has no controls and needs no script beyond generating the points.

whenToUse: While a view or part of one loads and nothing can be shown yet.

whenNotToUse: Inside a button that is working. Set aria-busy="true" on the button, which draws its own.

components.name: split-button
components.title: Split button
components.purpose: A main action joined to a menu button that holds other ways to do the same thing.
whenToUse: When one action is right most of the time and two or more close alternatives are needed now and then, such as Start task and Start on a new branch.
When the alternatives are variations of the main action, so the reader would look for them beside it.
whenNotToUse: For actions that are not variations of one another. Use buttons, or a menu behind a button that names what they act on.
For a single alternative. Show it as a second button.
To choose a value that stays chosen. Use a select or a segmented control.
For an option that is on or off. Use a toggle button.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The default. Both halves are plain buttons.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The main action also carries gw-button--primary when it is the one main action of the view. The menu button stays a plain button, so the pair never shows two accent fills.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. The menu button is 44px wide.

accessibility: Use a div with gw-split-button, role="group" and an aria-label that names the main action. It holds the main action, then the menu button, then the menu, in that order.
The main action is a button with gw-button and gw-split-button__action. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. Pressing it never opens the menu.

The menu button is a button with gw-button and gw-split-button__toggle, popovertarget set to the menu's id and aria-haspopup="menu". It holds the chevron icon with aria-hidden="true" and its own name in a gw-visually-hidden span, such as More ways to start the task. The name is never the main action's label again.

The menu is the menu component, copied from its examples, with the same name as the menu button in its aria-label. Its items are other ways to do the main action. The main action itself is not repeated in it.
At most the main action is primary. Two primary halves fail the one-primary-action rule.

Tab reaches the main action and then the menu button. Enter and Space activate each. The browser opens and closes the menu, closes it on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the menu button. Arrow keys inside the menu are the menu component's.
When the action is unavailable, set disabled on both halves. While the main action runs, set aria-busy="true" on it, change its label to say what is happening, and set disabled on the menu button.
The component needs no script of its own.

components.name: split-panel
components.title: Split panel
components.purpose: Two labelled regions, a list and the detail of the row chosen in it, side by side at 768px and up and stacked below, each scrolling by itself.
whenToUse: When the reader moves through a list and reads each item at length without losing their place: runs and their summaries, changed files and their diffs.
As the main content of a view, inside a shell that gives it a height, with the fill modifier.
With a list or a tree in the list region and any content in the detail region.
whenNotToUse: For a few facts about the selected row beside a list that scrolls with the page. Use the inspector.
For navigation beside the page. Use the sidebar layout with the sidebar nav.
Where the detail is a task that needs the whole phone screen, such as a transcript. Make the row a link to a view of its own below 768px.
For regions the reader must resize. The split is fixed, and there is no drag handle.

Each region scrolls by itself. A region with no focusable content, as a detail of plain text often is, takes tabindex="0" so the keyboard can scroll it. A region that holds links or buttons does not need it.

components.name: stepper
components.title: Stepper
components.purpose: Where the reader is in a short, fixed sequence of named steps: which are completed, which is current and which are still to come.
whenToUse: At the top of a flow of three to five steps that happen in a fixed order, such as connecting a repository.
To show how far a staged job has got, such as a release, where each stage has a name.
whenNotToUse: For progress with no named steps. Use the progress component.
For a record of what already happened, with times. Use the timeline.
For views the reader may open in any order. Use tabs.
For more than five steps, or steps that change with earlier answers. Say Step 3 of 8 in the view's heading and leave the stepper out.
For a flow of two fields. Put both in one form.

variants.name: default

The name is a span with gw-stepper__label. On a completed step it is an a element with the same class, underlined, that goes back to that step. The current and the upcoming steps are never links.
When every step is done the flow is over. Replace the stepper with the result, since no step carries aria-current any longer.
When the current step fails, keep aria-current on it, say so in its description, and put an alert below the stepper that says what happened and what to do.

Under an empty transcript, to show what can be asked of this repository or task.
whenNotToUse: For the view's actions, such as Start task or Stop. Use buttons.
For a choice among fixed options that stays selected. Use a select or radio inputs.
For an answer the agent is waiting on. Use an approval.
When there are no specific prompts to offer. Render nothing: a generic chip is worse than none.

accessibility: Use a ul with the class gw-suggestion-chips and an aria-label such as Suggested prompts, with one li per chip. A screen reader then announces the group and how many chips it holds.
